jobs.title: Mid Market Account Executive
jobs.excerpt: Avante is the enterprise AI platform for benefits teams.
jobs.description:
Avante is the enterprise AI platform for benefits teams. Benefits is one of the most complex, high-stakes functions in any company, and Avante’s purpose-built agents take on end-to-end benefits work, from checking vendor contracts against claims to preparing leadership reports to helping employees use and understand their benefits. Samsung Semiconductor, Real Chemistry, Zscaler and News Corp use Avante today to keep costs in check, support employees across the globe, and get more from their benefits investment.

The Role

You'll own the full deal, from first conversation through signature, and land new logos like Calix, Personify, Datavant, and Real Chemistry. Deals run $50K to $150K in ACV, move faster than enterprise, and involve smaller buying groups: typically a Head of Benefits or Total Rewards as champion, an HR or finance executive as economic buyer, and an IT or security reviewer.

Your hardest job is explaining how Avante differs from the ben admin platform, the decision support tool, and the point solutions buyers already own. Avante replaces none of them. It's the intelligence layer that connects them. Most of your pipeline will be direct, and when a broker or consultant is in the deal, you'll work alongside them without losing the buyer relationship.

This role reports to the Director of Sales. We're hiring someone 3–6 years into a quota-carrying career who is ready to own a full patch and a full cycle, with a path toward larger accounts as Avante scales.

What You'll Do

  • Own a named mid-market patch end-to-end. Build the territory plan, prioritize accounts, run the cycles, and close the business.
  • Generate your own pipeline. Work with Sales Development on outbound, and run your own research, outreach, and follow-up on your patch.
  • Run a fast, focused cycle. Move from discovery to demo to proposal with a mutual plan and dates the buyer agrees to. Identify the champion, economic buyer, and security reviewer early.
  • Sell the closed-loop story. Teach buyers what benefits intelligence is, why the loop between Carly and Ava matters, and why purpose-built agents beat generic AI bolted onto legacy systems.
  • Run sharp demos and proofs of value. Partner with Sales Engineering to get customers live in about 30 days.
  • Forecast with discipline. Keep a clean pipeline, use MEDDPICC or equivalent scaled to deal size, and bring risks forward early.
  • Use AI daily. Research accounts, draft outbound, prep meetings, and turn call transcripts into next steps with tools like Claude and Granola. If you're a traditional AE who occasionally tries ChatGPT, this isn't the right seat.
  • Adapt as we grow. Your patch, playbook, and deal size will evolve, and you should welcome that.

What We're Looking For

  • 3–6 years of quota-carrying SaaS sales experience, with at least 2 years closing new-logo deals at $50K+ ACV
  • A track record of hitting or exceeding quota while managing many concurrent opportunities
  • Experience building your own pipeline through outbound prospecting
  • Experience selling to HR, Benefits, or Finance buyers, with the presence to engage a Head of Benefits or a CFO
  • Comfort selling a new type of product where you have to teach the buyer what it is first
  • Active, hands-on use of AI in your selling motion
  • A methodical approach to pipeline, forecast, and qualification (MEDDPICC or equivalent)

Nice to Have

  • Experience selling into benefits, HR tech, or healthcare to self-funded employers
  • Experience selling AI-native or data-intensive platforms
  • Relationships with benefits leaders or the brokers and consultants who advise mid-market employers
  • Early-stage startup experience helping build the playbook

What We Offer

The compensation for this role is $250,000-$300,000 OTE. Where you land in that range depends on your experience, your skills, and how well your background fits what the role needs.

We also offer:

  • Equity: Stock options, so you share in what we’re building
  • Health coverage: Medical, dental, and vision, with employee premiums covered by Avante
  • Unlimited PTO: Take the time you need to rest and recharge, plus paid company holidays
  • Retirement: 401(k)
  • Commuter benefit: $150/month toward however you prefer to get to work

Avante is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We’re building a diverse, inclusive team and welcome candidates of all backgrounds.

How We Work

Our four values aren't aspirational. They translate into concrete operating tenets that shape how we make decisions every day.

Beat Yesterday. We re-evaluate our own toolkit every quarter, because the workflows that made you effective three months ago may already be outdated. We act on 70% of the information rather than waiting for certainty. We timebox, execute, and iterate, getting work in front of real people quickly instead of polishing in isolation. And we own our output regardless of how we produced it. AI can get you 80% of the way there. Everything that goes out with your name on it is your responsibility to review, refine, and stand behind.

Embrace Type 2 Fun. We take on hard problems and find meaning in the work, even when it's uncomfortable. We assume good intent and follow up directly rather than venting in side channels. We celebrate wins loudly and specifically, naming the actual behavior so the whole team learns what great looks like. We are on by default, because we owe it to each other and to our customers to be available beyond what a regular corporate job would demand. And we do unscalable things today that build scalable advantages tomorrow: every hand-built account play and late-night proposal turnaround earns us the right to scale later.

Stay Hungry, Stay Curious. We expect everyone to be the expert on AI in their function before anyone asks them to be. The landscape changes weekly. When you learn something, teach it. Learn enough about adjacent functions to ask good questions. Ask the question you think is too basic, because in complex domains like benefits, the cost of a wrong assumption can be a lost account. And remember: curiosity without urgency is a hobby. Learning has to translate into action on a timeline that matches the opportunity.

Act Like an Owner. We say the uncomfortable thing early, raising missed commitments or quality gaps directly with the person within 48 hours. We surface problems when they're small, not the week they become a crisis. Customer-facing work gets priority, always. And we close the loop every time, because over-communication is a feature at our stage, not a bug.

jobs.description:
BryceTech is seeking experienced Administrative and Operations Managers to provide senior-level financial, comptroller, administrative, and program operations support to the Naval Surface Warfare Center, Port Hueneme Division (NSWC PHD). These positions will support the Government’s financial management and program execution objectives through financial analysis, budget development, operational coordination, process improvement, reporting, and customer support. The successful candidates will apply strong analytical, organizational, and management skills to help ensure the effective use of resources, accurate financial and program data, and timely completion of organizational requirements.

Responsibilities

  • Provide financial management, comptroller, administrative, and program operations support to NSWC PHD departments and program offices

  • Support department-wide financial planning, budget development, resource allocation, expenditure tracking, and financial reporting

  • Analyze historical, current, and projected expenditures, commitments, and obligations to support operating budgets, carryover estimates, and funding decisions

  • Prepare budget justifications, financial impact statements, variance explanations, executive summaries, and other reports for Government review

  • Review financial transactions, funding documents, invoices, vouchers, and accounting records for accuracy, completeness, and compliance with applicable policies and procedures

  • Reconcile financial data across Government systems, research unmatched disbursements and accounting discrepancies, and coordinate corrective actions

  • Track funding status across multiple appropriation types and support the processing, monitoring, and closeout of funding documentation

  • Develop and maintain financial tools, metrics, spreadsheets, reports, and dashboards to support organizational decision-making and performance monitoring

  • Support the preparation and presentation of quarterly financial reviews, management briefings, and other executive-level materials

  • Interpret and apply financial management policies, procedures, regulations, and internal controls to support organizational objectives and regulatory compliance

  • Coordinate administrative and operational activities, including training requests, procurement requests, purchase requisitions, travel documentation, and related workflow requirements

  • Track program tasks, milestones, deliverables, schedules, risks, and resource requirements; prepare status reports and recommend actions to address issues or delays

  • Collect, analyze, and communicate program and operational data, identifying trends, challenges, and opportunities to improve organizational effectiveness

  • Develop, update, and maintain standard operating procedures, desk guides, memorandums, financial plans, program documentation, and training materials

  • Support continuous process improvement, business transformation, strategic planning, and quality management initiatives

  • Coordinate with Government customers, department personnel, external stakeholders, and other support teams to resolve issues and facilitate effective communication

  • Organize and facilitate meetings, prepare agendas and briefing materials, maintain schedules and calendars, and document meeting outcomes and action items

  • Support records management, document control, and the appropriate handling, storage, archiving, and disposition of Government information

  • Support department-level website and portal management, including content updates, user access management, newsletters, and reporting metrics, as assigned

  • Coordinate the operation and scheduling of Government conference facilities and secure and unclassified video teleconference capabilities, as assigned

  • Active Secret security clearance or above

  • Master’s degree from an accredited college or university

  • At least 10 years of relevant professional experience in financial management, comptroller operations, program management, business operations, or administrative support

  • Demonstrated experience analyzing financial, budgetary, operational, or program data and preparing reports and recommendations for management

  • Experience supporting budget development, financial tracking, resource allocation, accounting processes, or program execution

  • Ability to interpret and apply organizational policies, procedures, financial management principles, and applicable regulations

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare executive-level reports, presentations, and briefing materials

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word, and PowerPoint

  • Ability to manage competing priorities, coordinate multiple activities, identify operational challenges, and recommend practical solutions

  • Strong organizational, analytical, problem-solving, and customer service skills

Position is contingent upon contract award.

BryceTech offers a full range of benefits, including competitive salary, a comprehensive health plan including dental and vision coverage, company-paid life & disability insurance policies, 401(k) plan with company match, and an educational reimbursement program.

Our clients – including NASA, DoD, HHS, DHS, and other civil and national security agencies – rely on us to drive mission success and accelerate innovation.

jobs.excerpt: Chief Transformation Officer (CTO) – Insurance & Investments 1.
jobs.description:
Chief Transformation Officer (CTO) – Insurance & Investments

1. Role Summary

The Chief Transformation Officer (CTO) is responsible for leading enterprise-wide transformation initiatives to improve organizational performance, operational efficiency, business agility, and long-term competitiveness across the insurance and investment businesses.

The role involves developing and executing the organization's transformation strategy, modernizing business models, optimizing operating structures, driving digital adoption, and leading strategic change programs. The CTO will work closely with the CEO, Board, and executive leadership team to translate corporate strategy into measurable transformation outcomes.

The ideal candidate will combine strategic leadership, financial and operational expertise, technology awareness, and strong change management capabilities, with a proven track record of delivering complex transformation initiatives in insurance, investment management, banking, or financial services.

2. Key Responsibilities

Enterprise Transformation Strategy

  • Develop and execute the organization's enterprise-wide transformation strategy and roadmap.
  • Identify opportunities to improve business performance, operational effectiveness, profitability, and organizational agility.
  • Align transformation priorities with corporate strategy, market conditions, and long-term business objectives.
  • Evaluate existing business models, organizational structures, and operating processes to identify improvement opportunities.
  • Establish transformation objectives, milestones, governance frameworks, and measurable success criteria.

Business Model & Operating Model Transformation

  • Lead initiatives to modernize business models, operating structures, and service delivery frameworks.
  • Drive organizational restructuring, process redesign, and business integration initiatives.
  • Improve operational efficiency across insurance underwriting, claims, policy administration, distribution, and customer service.
  • Support transformation of investment operations, portfolio reporting, client servicing, and wealth management processes, where applicable.
  • Develop scalable operating models to support business expansion, diversification, and organizational growth.

Digital & Technology Transformation

  • Lead technology-enabled business transformation initiatives in collaboration with the CIO, CTO, and CDO.
  • Drive adoption of automation, AI, advanced analytics, cloud solutions, and digital platforms.
  • Modernize legacy systems, enterprise applications, and operational infrastructure.
  • Oversee transformation programs involving InsurTech, FinTech, digital insurance, and investment platforms.
  • Ensure technology investments deliver measurable improvements in productivity, customer experience, and business performance.

Financial & Operational Performance Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to improve profitability, reduce operating costs, and optimize resource utilization.
  • Lead cost transformation, process efficiency, and productivity improvement programs.
  • Establish performance management frameworks and operational KPIs.
  • Evaluate transformation business cases, financial benefits, investment requirements, and expected returns.
  • Monitor cost savings, revenue improvements, and overall financial impact of transformation initiatives.

Organizational Change Management

  • Develop and implement change management strategies to support enterprise transformation.
  • Build organizational readiness and secure leadership and employee engagement.
  • Lead communication, training, and stakeholder engagement initiatives during transformation programs.
  • Address resistance to change and promote a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement.
  • Support leadership development and workforce transformation initiatives.

Customer & Business Experience Transformation

  • Drive initiatives to improve customer journeys and service delivery across insurance and investment businesses.
  • Collaborate with the Chief Experience Officer and commercial leadership to improve customer satisfaction, retention, and engagement.
  • Simplify customer onboarding, claims processing, policy renewals, investment transactions, and client servicing.
  • Promote customer-centric operating models and consistent service standards.
  • Use customer insights and analytics to identify transformation priorities.

Risk, Governance & Regulatory Transformation

  • Ensure transformation initiatives align with applicable insurance, investment, financial services, and corporate governance requirements.
  • Work with risk, compliance, legal, and internal audit teams to strengthen organizational controls.
  • Lead initiatives to improve regulatory reporting, risk management processes, and governance frameworks.
  • Assess transformation-related operational, financial, technology, and regulatory risks.
  • Establish appropriate controls and accountability throughout transformation programs.

Strategic Projects, M&A & Business Integration

  • Oversee major strategic transformation programs, including mergers, acquisitions, joint ventures, and post-merger integration.
  • Lead integration of business processes, systems, teams, and organizational structures following acquisitions.
  • Support new market entry, geographic expansion, and business diversification initiatives.
  • Coordinate cross-functional transformation projects involving multiple subsidiaries and business units.
  • Track project outcomes and ensure delivery of expected strategic and financial benefits.

Leadership & Stakeholder Management

  • Work closely with the CEO, Board, executive team, and business unit heads to establish transformation priorities.
  • Lead transformation offices, program directors, project managers, and cross-functional teams.
  • Establish transformation governance, reporting structures, and performance accountability.
  • Manage relationships with external consultants, technology partners, and implementation specialists.
  • Present transformation progress, business impact, risks, and strategic recommendations to executive leadership and the Board.

3. Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Finance, Economics, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field.
  • MBA or Master's degree in Business Strategy, Organizational Development, Finance, or Transformation Management preferred.
  • 12–15+ years of progressive experience in corporate strategy, business transformation, management consulting, operational excellence, or enterprise change management.
  • At least 5 years in a senior executive or leadership role overseeing large-scale transformation initiatives.
  • Significant experience in insurance, banking, investment management, asset management, wealth management, or financial services.
  • Proven track record of leading complex enterprise transformation programs with measurable financial and operational outcomes.
  • Strong understanding of insurance operations, investment services, financial products, and regulated business environments.
  • Experience in operating model redesign, organizational restructuring, digital transformation, and process optimization.
  • Strong financial acumen, strategic planning, and business performance management capabilities.
  • Excellent leadership, communication, stakeholder engagement, and change management skills.

Preferred Certifications:

  • Prosci Change Management Certification.
  • Certified Business Transformation Professional (CBTP).
  • PMP or Program Management Professional (PgMP).

- Lean Six Sigma Black Belt.

- Agile or Scrum certifications.

4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Achievement of enterprise transformation milestones.
  • Cost savings and operational efficiency improvements.
  • Revenue growth and profitability improvements resulting from transformation.
  • Reduction in process turnaround times and operational bottlenecks.
  • Successful implementation of new operating models and business processes.

- Digital adoption and automation rates.

  • Customer satisfaction and service delivery improvements.
  • Employee engagement and organizational change adoption.
  • Successful integration of acquired businesses and strategic partnerships.
  • Realization of expected transformation benefits and ROI.
  • Regulatory compliance and risk management effectiveness.
  • Delivery of transformation initiatives within approved budgets and timelines.

jobs.description:
Radar Reinvented.

Echodyne offers the world’s first compact solid-state true beam-steering radar for a wide range of industries and applications. Our high-performance radars work in all weather and are designed for autonomous vehicles, uncrewed aircraft & drones, and security of borders, critical infrastructure, and smart cities. The company combines the patented technology of metamaterials with powerful software to create a radar sensor with unprecedented performance at commercial price points. Echodyne offers its radars to companies working in Automotive, Transportation, Critical Infrastructure Protection, Border Security, Smart Cities, Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (UAS), and Airspace Management including Urban Air Mobility (UTM).

Echodyne is seeking a Sales Commissions Analyst to join our fast-growing team.

ROLE OVERVIEW

Echodyne is seeking a Sales Commissions Analyst to administer sales compensation plans and ensure accurate, timely commission and incentive payments. This role will partner with Sales Operations, Finance, and HR to manage monthly calculations, validate payouts, and help employees understand their compensation.

The ideal candidate is thorough, process-oriented, and highly skilled in Excel, with strong attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy. This role will also improve the tools and processes used to calculate, track, and report compensation as our go-to-market organization evolves.

This role has access to sensitive employee earnings, compensation plans, and financial information. Maintaining confidentiality and sharing information only with authorized individuals is a core responsibility.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Commission Administration and Accuracy

  • Administer sales compensation plans and monthly payout processes in accordance with approved plan terms.
  • Calculate and validate commissions, bonuses, and other sales incentive payments.
  • Reconcile sales, employee, and compensation data across systems to identify and resolve discrepancies.
  • Prepare payout summaries and supporting documentation for review, approval, and payroll processing.
  • Maintain clear records of calculations, adjustments, approvals, and payout history.
  • Resolve compensation inquiries and explain calculations and adjustments clearly.
  • Handle employee and compensation information with discretion and confidentiality.

Compensation Models and Plan Support

  • Maintain compensation models, payout logic, and employee plan assignments.
  • Support compensation plan development, implementation, and rollout using established best practices.
  • Support updates to plans as the go-to-market structure, territories, quotas, and sales roles evolve.
  • Model and validate proposed plan changes and their impact on payouts.
  • Document plan rules, calculation methods, and exceptions to support consistent administration.

Process Improvement and Reporting

  • Identify opportunities to simplify and automate compensation processes.
  • Improve the tools, workflows, and data models used to calculate, track, and report compensation.
  • Reduce manual effort and processing time while maintaining accuracy and appropriate review controls.
  • Develop recurring reports that provide visibility into commission earnings, payouts, and adjustments.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to improve source data quality and resolve recurring issues.

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 3 years+ (minimum) of experience in sales compensation, finance, sales operations, or a related analytical role.
  • Advanced Excel and data modeling skills, including complex formulas, lookup functions, pivot tables, and data reconciliation.
  • Thorough approach to work, with strong attention to detail and a high standard for accuracy.
  • Understanding of best practices for building, administering, and rolling out sales commission plans.
  • Process-oriented mindset, with the ability to document workflows, identify gaps, and implement improvements.
  • Ability to validate calculations across multiple data sources and investigate discrepancies.
  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to meet recurring monthly deadlines.
  • Clear communication skills and the ability to explain compensation calculations to employees and business partners.
  • Demonstrated ability to handle highly confidential employee and compensation information with discretion, protect sensitive data, and follow established access and information-sharing requirements.

PREFERRED SKILLS / EXPERIENCE

  • Direct experience working with sales compensation or financial data.
  • Familiarity with Salesforce, NetSuite, or sales compensation management tools.

SUCCESS IN THIS ROLE

  • Accurate, timely commission and incentive payouts, with clear supporting documentation.
  • Simplified compensation processes that reduce manual work, errors, and processing time.
  • Compensation models and payout logic that reflect approved plans and support revenue goals.
  • Improved tools and reporting that make compensation easier to calculate, track, and understand.
  • Timely resolution of compensation questions and discrepancies, building confidence in the payout process.

Echodyne’s technology is export controlled by the U.S. Government and we must evaluate an applicant’s eligibility to handle export-controlled information or obtain required Government authorizations.  Therefore, we will ask you as part of the application process to identify whether you are a U.S. Citizen or green card holder, or have asylum/refugee status in the U.S.

jobs.description:
About the Job
Title: Chief of Staff – Executive Operations
Location: Remote (US, Eastern or Central time zone)
Type: Full-time (W-2) or Part-time contractor (1099)
Compensation: $85,000–$105,000 annually (full-time) or $42–$55/hour (part-time, ~20 hours/week)
Start: April 2026

About Serve Freight

Serve Freight is a high-reliability logistics operator specializing in complex freight execution for mid-market shippers and project-driven industries. We manage transportation, warehousing, and value-added logistics programs for companies that cannot afford missed delivery windows, broken communication, or unreliable carriers. We are scaling fast in 2026 and building the operational infrastructure to support it. This role is part of that buildout.

The Role

We are hiring a Chief of Staff – Executive Operations to serve as the CEO’s operational right-hand, owning the day-to-day rhythm of the business so the CEO can focus on the things only he can do.

This is not a traditional Executive Assistant or operations management position. It is a hybrid role that combines structured operational ownership with cross-functional coordination, process ownership, and real decision-making authority.

You are the person who keeps the CEO out of the weeds. You own the recurring operational cadence, drive accountability on tactical priorities, and make the calls that would otherwise sit in a queue waiting for approval.

50% of your time will be structured operational ownership. 50% will be dedicated to cross-functional problem-solving, process improvement, and team coordination.

What You Will Do

Executive & Calendar Management

  • Manage the CEO’s calendar: scheduling, rescheduling, conflict resolution

• Triage and prioritize the CEO’s inbox

• Coordinate travel logistics

  • Prepare meeting agendas, pre-reads, and follow-up action items

Data, Dashboards & Financial Support

  • Pull and format weekly operational dashboards from Turvo, QuickBooks, and HubSpot
  • Run down accounts receivable discrepancies and flag issues
  • Prepare financial summaries and talking points for leadership meetings
  • Support the company’s strategic advisor with slide deck preparation and data pulls

Process & SOP Ownership

  • Draft and maintain internal SOPs for recurring operational processes
  • Document workflows across departments as they are formalized
  • Research and recommend operational tools within defined budget parameters
  • Integrate approved tools into existing workflows

Operational Problem-Solving

  • Investigate and resolve operational issues across departments before they reach the CEO
  • Triage which priorities you can own directly vs. what needs to be escalated
  • Reschedule initiative timelines when circumstances change
  • Coordinate with internal team members across operations, accounting, and brokerage

Decision-Making Authority

This role carries real decision-making responsibility within defined boundaries. You will not be waiting for approval on every task.

You will decide: which tools to investigate, which software to select within budget, how to reschedule internal timelines, how to triage and route requests, and how to resolve calendar conflicts.

You will escalate any commitments to external parties, expenditures above the threshold, changes to sales or pricing, and strategic or partnership decisions.

Who You Are

  • 5–8 years in operations, chief of staff, or executive support roles at a growing company (under 50 employees preferred)
  • Comfortable wearing multiple hats and operating across departments without waiting for a playbook
  • Can make decisions without perfect information; does not freeze with ambiguous direction
  • Strong written communicator: SOPs, slide decks, and emails without heavy editing
  • Data-literate: can pull and present operational and financial data without being an analyst
  • You think like an owner, not a task-taker

Tools You Will Use

Turvo (TMS), QuickBooks Online, HubSpot (CRM), Google Workspace, Slack, Notion, Excel/Sheets. You do not need to be an expert in all of these on day one, but you should be comfortable learning quickly.

What Success Looks Like

At 30 days: The CEO has measurably more free time. Recurring tasks are transferred and running on schedule.

At 60 days: You are proactively resolving issues before they reach the CEO. You have recommended or implemented at least one process improvement.

At 90 days: The CEO feels like you are an extension of himself. Internal stakeholders engage with you directly. Minimal oversight needed.

What This Role Is Not

• Not a calendar-only EA role

• Not a system administrator or IT role

  • Not a sales or business development role
  • Not a strategic advisory role -- but your judgment and recommendations will directly shape how we operate

How to Apply

Submit an application here and send a short note (not a cover letter) to with the subject line: Chief of Staff - Executive Operations - [Your Name].

Answer these three questions:

  • Tell us about a time you made a decision on behalf of an executive. What was the situation, what did you decide, and what happened?
  • Describe a process you built or improved at a previous company. What was broken, what did you change, and what was the result?
  • Give an example of a time you had to figure something out with almost no direction. How did you approach it?

No form letters. No AI-generated cover letters. We read every response.

Role Purpose

The Client Finance Manager is a senior leadership role, with oversight of one client account. This role oversees a geographically dispersed team, across multiple countries in EMEA regions. This role will have direct responsibility for leading the finance team.

The Client Finance Manager is the financial liaison between the JLL Operational Team and the Client. Responsible for the implementation and execution of accounting processes and programs designed to ensure the appropriate level of accuracy, tracking and control over the operating expenses and capital expenditures of the client account. They are also responsible for accounting compliance, and all JLL Corporate finance deliverables for the client account including budgeting, forecasting and monthly variance analysis.

POS-P2934

Solutions Engineer

AI is changing how businesses buy. Buyers arrive informed, often having researched with AI, and they no longer buy on promises: they want to see their own business running in HubSpot, and proof that it will deliver measurable results, before they commit. HubSpot's agentic customer platform is leading this shift, connecting customer context, Breeze AI agents and a unified CRM so scaling companies realize business outcomes, not just adopt software. As buying moves from large contracts signed up front to proving value one use case at a time, we are building a new technical go-to-market team to lead customers through that change.

Come join the team defining what technical go-to-market looks like in the AI era. As a Solutions Engineer, you bring a customer-facing background in solutions engineering, solutions architecture or technical consulting, along with hands-on building experience. You won't just show customers what's possible; you'll build it with them, prove it delivers their outcomes, and set them on the path to realizing them. This is a pre-sales role, not a software engineering role, for technologists who build fast with AI tools. Few companies have figured out how to sell this way at scale, and here you will help lead the industry in defining and building a new technical go-to-market model that others will follow. If you love building, thrive at the intersection of business and technology, and want to help write the playbook for how software is bought next, this role is for you.

In this role, you will need to:

  • Tell compelling, outcome-led stories (via demos and product led experiences) that show customers how their business can be reimagined on HubSpot's agentic customer platform.
  • Lead discovery that uncovers the pain, outcomes and requirements by engaging customers and then earning the right to go deeper
  • Partner with Account Executives to map the technical buying committee, competitive landscape and path to a decision.
  • Redesign customers' legacy complexity into a simplified HubSpot architecture that integrates with their wider tech stack.
  • Design and build working proofs quickly with AI coding tools, Breeze AI agents and the HubSpot developer framework, scoped to clear use cases, success criteria and timelines.
  • Run hands-on proofs with customers, iterating on their feedback and clearing security and integration risks to secure the technical win.
  • Turn proof into a business case, ROI and use-case roadmap with a consumption plan that sizes the first commitment.
  • Present results to executives and generate confidence to move forward with HubSpot
  • Guide and build with customers and implementation partners to ensure the realization of the customer’s first outcomes.
  • Create reusable assets and capture field feedback to shape our playbooks and the HubSpot product roadmap
  • Occasional travel to customer sites to perform the above activities
  • Success measurement: This role will be measured on our ability to win new customers and ensure that the customer achieves their initial business outcomes

We are looking for people who (skills and experience):

  • Experience: Customer-facing background in solutions engineering, solutions architecture, technical consulting or implementation for SaaS platforms, with a track record of winning complex deals or delivering solutions that moved business results.
  • Art-of-the-Possible Storytelling & Discovery: Ability to turn a customer's goals into a compelling, outcome-led vision of their business reimagined in HubSpot, backed by peer proof rather than features. jobs.excerpt: About ToptalToptal is a global network of top talent in business, design, and technology that enables companies to scale their teams, on-demand.
jobs.description:
About Toptal

Toptal is a global network of top talent in business, design, and technology that enables companies to scale their teams, on-demand. With $200+ million in annual revenue and team members based around the globe, Toptal is the world’s largest fully remote workforce.

We take the best elements of virtual teams and combine them with a support structure that encourages innovation, social interaction, and fun. We see no borders, move at a fast pace, and are never afraid to break the mold.

Job Summary:

As an SMB Sales Development Representative (SDR), you will drive business growth by opening new opportunities with small and midsize businesses and by bringing back clients who have gone quiet. You’ll play a pivotal role in identifying potential customers, generating new business opportunities, and providing support to both customers and our team. You will work three motions: cold outreach to a prioritized list of companies with $5M to $300M in annual revenue, reactivation of dormant clients, and call backs to prospects who missed a scheduled Client Advisor call. You will set the stage for successful sales interactions through outreach and nurturing relationships to secure qualified meetings for our SMB sales team. If you are a self motivated individual with a passion for sales, we encourage you to join our team!

This is a remote position. We do not offer visa sponsorship or assistance. Applicants must be authorized to work in the US at the time of hire. Resumes and communication must be submitted in English.

Responsibilities:

The following information is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or required skills.

  • Exercise discretion and independent judgment.
  • Sales: Understand current and future demand across the SMB and midmarket segments. Enable, educate, and directly support the sales force to best position Toptal with SMB clients and win new business. Lead client conversations, presenting Toptal’s perspective on innovation and talent topics, and ask exploratory questions to better understand client needs.
  • Begin the Relationship: Through lead generation activities and cold calling, you will prospect, educate, qualify, and develop sales ready leads and opportunities from a prioritized list of companies with $5M to $300M in annual revenue. You will enthusiastically explain Toptal’s vision, pinpoint opportunities, and generate interest.
  • Reactivate and Recover: You will restart relationships that have gone quiet. When a dormant client has not restarted an engagement with its Account Manager, the account moves to the SDR pool, and you reach out, book the meeting, and bring the client back. You will also call back prospects who missed a scheduled Client Advisor call, starting 7 days after the missed call, and book a new meeting.
  • Client and Industry Knowledge: Clients are at the heart of everything we do. As the first point of contact for future SMB clients, you will build rapport through strategic outreach and a well rounded client and industry knowledge. Researching clients and staying informed on industry trends will be key to your success.
  • Collaborate with Team Members: You will collaborate with your team, SMB outbound Account Executives, Account Managers, and Client Advisors to pursue opportunities, recommend appropriate follow up actions, and schedule qualified meetings. Account Executives close the opportunities you source, and Account Managers take over each account once the engagement starts. Communicating via Zoom and Slack is critical to maintaining a high level of collaboration and clear communication within the team.
  • Growth and Development: Our team has an aversion to complacency. We are always looking to improve both individually and as a team. Being open to and implementing feedback will be critical success factors in this role and at Toptal. As you become more comfortable in the role, you will help evolve our demand generation strategy and tactics.

In the first week, expect to:

  • Onboard and integrate into Toptal.
  • Learn Toptal’s model, our value proposition, and our story.
  • Work with cross functional teams to understand how you can utilize our incredible global team to build client relationships and drive success.
  • Learn the breadth of Toptal’s impact on companies of every size, from fast growing SMBs to the world’s largest enterprises.
  • Grasp the importance of the SDR function to the success of Toptal.
  • Understand our sales method and our selling process to set you up for success.

In the first month, expect to:

  • Complete our personalized sales training program with mock calls, cold calls, and role play scenarios.
  • Learn how to use Salesforce.com (our CRM) and our outreach and productivity tools (ZoomInfo, SalesLoft, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, Nooks, and Claude).
  • Integrate into your pod, partner with SMB outbound Account Executives, Account Managers, and Client Advisors, and begin working your prioritized account list.
  • Learn the process for each motion: new business outreach, dormant client reactivation, and missed call follow up. Implement an outreach process and hit your first month objectives.
  • Learn how to analyze industry drivers, business problems, and target buyers.

In the first three months, expect to:

  • Complete your ramp on the SDR team and attain your metrics, which include calls, emails, Sales Accepted Leads (SALs), and pipeline created.
  • Exercising discretion and independent judgment, uncover new opportunities within target accounts, dormant clients, and missed call leads that result in revenue generating engagements for Toptal.
  • Hit activity, SAL, and pipeline objectives.
  • Become proficient in using our sales tools.
  • Learn how to maintain excellent data integrity in Salesforce.com.

In the first six months, expect to:

  • Continuously hit fully ramped quotas and objectives.
  • Assist with training and onboarding new SDRs.
  • Build new and existing client relationships, bring dormant clients back, and continue to execute account plans.
  • Suggest, implement, and experiment with new lead and demand generation activities.

In the first year, expect to:

  • Have built a portfolio of net new accounts from the prioritized account list, alongside clients brought back through reactivation and missed call follow up.
  • Become a mentor to new members of the team, helping them learn about Toptal, our model, and how proper sales development practices can improve relationships and increase revenue.

Qualifications and Job Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree is required.
  • 1 to 3 years of experience as an SDR or outbound Account Executive in SMB or midmarket sales.
  • Knowledgeable. Broad understanding of business challenges encountered by small and midsize businesses.
  • Critical thinking. Critically think through the challenges clients face to create new opportunities from target accounts, dormant clients, and missed call leads.
  • Perseverance. Be relentless and push towards your goal.
  • Passion. Enthusiasm and ambition to succeed in this role, as it can be difficult if you hate rejection.
  • Curiosity. A desire to understand people, their problems, their companies, and their industries.
  • Conscientiousness. We’re not doing a simple SaaS sale, so discussions may get technical. Understanding sophisticated issues and explaining them to clients is important.
  • Motivated. Be highly motivated and continuously strive for personal and professional improvement.
  • Resourceful. Think about target accounts as your own business. We want self starters who are passionate about hunting for new accounts, and who thrive with the freedom and accountability of leading their portion of the business.
  • Proactive. Understand our mission and do the work required to drive us to that goal, by following a process and being creative.
  • Urgency. SMB deals move fast. You follow up quickly on every lead, reactivation, and missed call.
  • Communication. You must exhibit outstanding written and verbal communication skills. Communication is the lifeblood of both internal and external relationships. Demonstrate excellent communication in all forms, across a wide variety of personality types, roles, and geographies.
  • Team. Nothing we do is done in isolation. Success depends on your ability to work as a team both within Toptal and within your client accounts.
  • Ownership. Exhibit ownership of accounts, successes, and failures.
  • Problem Solver. Life throws in minor challenges beyond the primary problems this role is meant to solve. You must have the ability to take those in stride and persist despite setbacks.
  • Prioritization. The nature of this role requires that you understand the priorities and timelines associated with each of your accounts and execute appropriately with those in mind.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, rapidly growing company and handle a wide variety of challenges, deadlines, and a diverse array of contacts.
  • You must be a world-class individual contributor to thrive at Toptal. You will not be here just to tell other people what to do.

Essential Job Functions

  • Regularly and reliably attend scheduled virtual team meetings on camera.
  • Work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Use all required digital collaboration tools.
  • Prioritize and self-manage workflows and deadlines.

US FLSA Classification: Full-Time/Exempt

This position receives a base salary and is also eligible to earn monthly commissions based on sales development results. For candidates who meet the qualifications and job requirements listed above, Individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

Applications are accepted on an ongoing basis. In the US, Toptal’s benefit offerings include participation in a 401(k) retirement plan; medical, dental, and vision health insurance plans; basic life insurance coverage and short-term and long-term disability coverage; access to flexible spending, dependent care, and health savings accounts; access to telehealth virtual doctors; an employee assistance program; and flexible paid time off.

Job Description: Director of PMO – Insurance & Investments

1. Role Summary

The Director of Project Management Office (PMO) is responsible for establishing, leading, and managing the organization's Project Management Office to ensure effective governance, planning, execution, monitoring, and delivery of strategic and operational projects.

The role oversees the project portfolio across insurance, investment, corporate operations, technology, digital transformation, and business development functions. The Director of PMO ensures projects are delivered within approved timelines, budgets, quality standards, and organizational objectives while maintaining effective risk management, resource allocation, and stakeholder engagement.

The successful candidate will drive project management excellence, strengthen governance frameworks, improve delivery performance, and ensure that project outcomes contribute to business growth, operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and customer experience.

2. Key Responsibilities

A. PMO Strategy, Leadership & Governance

  • Establish, develop, and lead the organization's Project Management Office.
  • Define PMO strategy, policies, methodologies, standards, and governance frameworks.
  • Implement standardized project management processes, tools, templates, and reporting structures.
  • Establish project approval processes, stage gates, escalation procedures, and accountability frameworks.
  • Promote project management best practices across departments and business units.
  • Ensure alignment between project execution and corporate strategy.

B. Project Portfolio Management

  • Oversee the organization's project portfolio, ensuring alignment with strategic priorities.
  • Evaluate project proposals, business cases, feasibility studies, and investment requirements.
  • Prioritize projects based on business value, financial impact, risk, and resource availability.
  • Monitor project dependencies, interdepartmental coordination, and portfolio-level risks.
  • Provide recommendations to senior management regarding project prioritization and resource allocation.
  • Track portfolio performance and ensure delivery of expected business benefits.

C. Project Planning & Execution

  • Oversee the planning, scheduling, budgeting, and execution of strategic projects.
  • Ensure project managers develop comprehensive project plans, milestones, deliverables, and resource requirements.
  • Monitor project progress and identify delays, delivery challenges, and performance gaps.
  • Drive corrective actions and escalation processes to maintain project delivery commitments.
  • Ensure projects are completed within approved scope, budget, timelines, and quality standards.
  • Coordinate cross-functional teams to ensure smooth project implementation.

D. Insurance & Investment Project Oversight

  • Oversee projects related to insurance operations, underwriting, claims management, policy administration, and distribution.
  • Coordinate initiatives involving investment operations, financial products, portfolio reporting, and client services, where applicable.
  • Support the implementation of regulatory, compliance, risk management, and internal control initiatives.
  • Monitor projects involving new product development, market expansion, operational improvements, and business integration.
  • Ensure project deliverables reflect the operational and regulatory requirements of the insurance and financial services industry.

E. Digital Transformation & Technology Projects

  • Oversee technology-enabled transformation projects, including core insurance systems, CRM, ERP, digital platforms, and automation initiatives.
  • Coordinate with IT, technology, operations, and business teams to ensure successful implementation.

If we make a mistake, we own up to it right away and do what it takes to make it right. Our dedication to security and compliance is key to earning trust, fighting fraud and ultimately, our success.

Description

AWS Cloud Engineer

Location: US / Canada (Eastern Time) - Home based

About AllCloud

AllCloud is a leader in amplifying organizations’ cloud potential through AI. With a track record of hundreds of successful migrations and implementations across AWS and Salesforce, AllCloud has developed strategies and solutions that enable businesses of all sizes to remain at the forefront of innovation.

AllCloud is a leader in AI-led professional and managed services. As an AWS Premier and audited managed services Partner, and Salesforce Consulting partner, AllCloud provides comprehensive AI-led cloud journey support, from initial migration to ongoing management through our Engage Managed Services. Our expertise ensures that clients remain aligned with ecosystem best practices while focusing on their core business growth.

AllCloud serves clients across the globe with offices in EMEA and North America. www.allcloud.io

﻿

Job Summary

AllCloud is seeking an AWS Cloud Engineer to design, build, and deploy highly scalable, reliable, and secure cloud environments for our customers. In this role, you will focus on delivering complex cloud projects, including large-scale migrations from on-premises data centers to AWS, containerized application deployment (including Amazon EKS), building new landing zones, and implementing infrastructure-as-code using modern automation frameworks. You will be responsible for setting up, maintaining, and evolving AWS architectures; developing automation to streamline delivery; ensuring robust monitoring, alerting, and troubleshooting practices; and leveraging cutting-edge AWS services to help customers achieve their business goals. This position is hands-on, customer-facing, and integral to driving successful AWS delivery engagements.

Requirements

Summary of Key Responsibilities

  • Architect, design, deploy, and maintain scalable, highly available, and secure AWS infrastructure for project needs (e.g., compute, storage, networking, database).
  • Lead or participate in cloud migrations: lifting and shifting on-premises workloads, re-architecting to cloud-native services.
  • Build and maintain Infrastructure as Code (IaC) using tools such as Terraform, AWS CloudFormation, AWS CDK.
  • Implement CI/CD pipelines (for example via AWS CodePipeline / AWS CodeBuild / Jenkins / GitLab CI) to automate deployment workflows.
  • Implement serverless solutions using AWS Lambda, Step Functions, and integrate event-driven architectures where appropriate.
  • Containerize applications (Docker) and orchestrate microservices using AWS container platform services, with a strong focus on Amazon EKS, ECS, and Fargate.
  • Ensure monitoring, logging, alerting, tracing of AWS resources and applications using tools like CloudWatch, X-Ray, Prometheus, Grafana, ELK/EFK stack.
  • Apply best practices around security: IAM policies, least privilege, encryption (at rest/in transit), network segmentation (VPCs, subnets), Web Application Firewall (WAF), GuardDuty, AWS Shield, etc.
  • Implement backup, disaster recovery and high availability strategies; manage data redundancies, snapshots, multi-AZ / multi-region architectures.
  • Optimize cost & performance: right-sizing resources, identifying waste, designing for efficiency.
  • Troubleshoot, debug, and resolve issues in cloud infrastructure and services; conduct root cause analyses.
  • Maintain documentation for architectures, configurations, standard operating procedures, runbooks.
  • Engage with cross-functional teams: developers, QA, operations, security/compliance, and project managers to ensure successful delivery.
  • Communicate proactively and effectively with clients to understand technical needs, provide progress updates, and articulate complex solutions clearly.
  • Apply critical thinking and strategic problem-solving to evaluate trade-offs, identify root causes, and design robust cloud architectures.
  • Stay up to date on the latest AWS services, features, industry best practices; evaluate new technologies and recommend improvements.
  • Perform deep OS-level troubleshooting and system administration across both Linux and Windows environments operating in the cloud.

Summary of Requirements & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Technology or relevant field (or equivalent work experience).
  • 3-5+ years of hands-on experience working with AWS in an engineering or infrastructure role (seniority adjustable).
  • Strong knowledge of core AWS services: EC2, S3, VPC, RDS / Aurora, Lambda, API Gateway, IAM, CloudWatch, etc.
  • Proven experience with Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools: Terraform, AWS CloudFormation, or AWS CDK.
  • Hands-on experience with containerization and orchestration using Docker, Kubernetes / Amazon EKS, ECS, and Fargate.
  • Proven ability to debug and troubleshoot complex container workload issues in Kubernetes, Amazon EKS, and AWS ECS environments.
  • Experience building CI/CD pipelines using tools such as Jenkins, GitLab CI/CD, AWS CodePipeline, GitHub Actions.
  • Solid scripting skills (Python, Bash, NodeJS, PowerShell, or similar) for automating tasks.
  • Working familiarity with monitoring, logging, tracing tools (e.g. CloudWatch, X-Ray, ELK stack, Prometheus, Grafana).
  • Strong understanding of cloud networking, security, and compliance (VPCs, subnets, security groups, network ACLs, encryption, identity management).
  • Experience in project delivery: working in agile or scrum environments, estimating work, delivering against milestones.
  • Excellent analytical, problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
  • Good communication skills—able to explain complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Deep technical knowledge and hands-on experience with OS-level administration, configuration, and advanced troubleshooting for both Linux and Windows Server platforms.
  • Strong client-facing communication skills with a proven track record of building trust and managing technical discussions with stakeholders.
  • Exceptional critical thinking, analytical reasoning, and decisive problem-solving capabilities under complex or ambiguous scenario conditions.

Why work for us?

Our team inspires progress in each other and in our customers through our relentless pursuit of excellence; you will work with leaders who promote learning and personal development.

jobs.excerpt: At EQT, you won't just do a job, you'll help shape our future.
jobs.description:
At EQT, you won't just do a job, you'll help shape our future. Through Transparent Leadership, you'll work alongside leaders who value collaboration and ensure every voice is heard. Through Connected Impact, you'll see how your work influences critical business decisions and drives value across our operations. Through Supported Growth, you'll have opportunities to expand your skills through cross-functional collaboration, development opportunities, and career advancement. Join our Qrew!

EQT is building a fleet of AI agents that work alongside our people, and we need an AI Engineer to help it grow. You'll join an AI team that builds the shared tools agents rely on, configures and deploys the agents themselves, and keeps the whole fleet healthy once it's live.

Our agents already run in production on Microsoft Foundry, posting into Salesforce and the enterprise systems our people use every day. The next step is scale: many more agents, built faster, with business users helping tune them.

As an AI Engineer, you build and maintain the capabilities our agents run on, and you monitor and optimize the agent fleet once it's in production. You set up the configuration for each prompt agent and customize its tools. Then you hand off to AI Specialists and domain experts, who test against real cases and tune the prompts until the agent is right.

When reasoning alone can't do the job reliably, you build a pro-code hosted agent or specialized tooling. That's the exception, not the plan.

Who thrives here:

  • You think agentically. You trust reasoning models to do most of the heavy lifting, and you reach for deterministic code where the outcome must be guaranteed, not by default.
  • You build for flexibility. You'd rather ship an agent that improves as models get better and cheaper than hardcode every scenario and fall behind.
  • You favor progress over perfection. You'd rather get many useful agents live and improve them than polish one forever.
  • You make others better. You enjoy building the tools and patterns that let business users and new builders do more on their own.
  • You're excited about where AI is going. You follow the field, try new models and tools as they land, and want to help an organization change how it works.

The AI Engineer I/II/III responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Build and maintain shared agent tools and capabilities.
  • Configure Foundry prompt agents: instructions, model selection, tool assignments, permissions, and guardrails, ready for others to test and tune.
  • Customize and extend tools when an agent needs something the shared set doesn't yet cover.
  • Partner with AI Specialists and domain experts as they test against real cases, and coach them on prompt design and evaluation.
  • Deploy agents and monitor the fleet through the Foundry control plane: evaluations, monitoring and alerts, audit trail, and cost.
  • Optimize agents in production, and recognize when a deployment is drifting or needs tighter guardrails, better data, or a narrower scope.
  • Build pro-code hosted agents or specialized tooling when review shows a prompt agent can't do the job reliably.
  • Ensure agents adhere to our security and identity standards.
  • Help shape the Agent Factory standards and share what you learn, so the next agent is faster to build than the last.
  • Stay current with models, agent frameworks, and Foundry features, and bring forward ideas that move more work from code to reasoning.

Required Experience and Skills:

  • Bachelor's degree in a technical discipline (computer science, engineering, information systems, or similar), or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • 3+ years of professional experience in software engineering, data engineering, or AI/ML roles.
  • Hands-on experience building LLM-based agents or applications: prompt design, tool calling, retrieval, and evaluating outputs against real cases.
  • Solid software engineering fundamentals in Python, including git, code review, testing, and working with APIs.
  • Working experience with Microsoft Azure or a similar cloud platform, including identity, permissions, and secrets management.
  • Comfort working across enterprise systems and data, including SQL and integrating with platforms like Salesforce and Databricks.
  • Judgment about when code is the right answer versus when a well-designed prompt and the right tools are simpler and just as successful.
  • Clear communicator who can explain technical tradeoffs to business partners and coach non-engineers as they test and tune agents.

Preferred Experience and Skills:

  • Experience with Microsoft Foundry (Azure AI Foundry): prompt agents, hosted agents, tools, evaluations, and the control plane.
  • Exposure to agent frameworks and protocols such as Model Context Protocol (MCP), LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, or similar.
  • Working knowledge of Salesforce (configuration, security model, Flow) and the Databricks ecosystem (Unity Catalog, Databricks SQL).
  • Experience operating AI in production: monitoring, evaluation harnesses, cost tracking, and responsible AI practices such as PII handling, guardrails, and human-in-the-loop review.

Remote work is being considered for this role excluding the following states: California, Connecticut, Delaware, Illinois, Indiana, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Michigan, New Jersey, New York, and Tennessee unless willing to relocate.

Selected incumbent will be placed into the position that best suits their abilities and experience level.

jobs.excerpt: 以下为中文版本Role OverviewExperience focus 5–7 yearsYou will own the product direction, priorities and measurable outcomes of an assigned mobile game or substantial product area.
jobs.description:
以下为中文版本

Role Overview

Experience focus 5–7 years

You will own the product direction, priorities and measurable outcomes of an assigned mobile game or substantial product area. You will connect player insight, game design and commercial goals, then work with the team to turn those choices into releases, experiments and product improvements.

You will work closely with Game Design, UX, Art, Engineering, QA, Analytics, User Acquisition, Monetization and Finance, as well as publishing or development partners where relevant. You will lead through clear decisions and cross-functional coordination, with budgets and approval authority defined for your product scope.

I. KEY JOB DUTIES

1. Product strategy and player discovery

  • Define target players, product problems and priorities using market research, competitor analysis, player feedback and behavioral data.
  • Build business cases and maintain an outcome-led roadmap. Compare player value, commercial potential, effort and risk, and explain what to build, defer or stop.
  • Plan discovery, prototypes and playtests to test important assumptions before larger investment. Update recommendations when evidence changes.

2. Gameplay and monetization

  • Partner with Game Design and UX to improve the core loop, onboarding, difficulty, progression and session experience for the intended audience.
  • Evaluate economy sources and sinks, reward pacing, ad placements and purchase offers with specialists. Apply the systems relevant to the game.
  • Balance revenue opportunities with retention, progression and player experience. Validate changes and investigate unintended effects.

3. Product analytics and experimentation

  • Define product metrics, tracking requirements and data-quality checks. Use cohort and funnel analysis to investigate player behavior and performance changes.
  • Set testable hypotheses, primary measures, guardrails and decision criteria. Review experiment validity and uncertainty with analysts, then decide whether to roll out, iterate or stop.

4. Feature specification and delivery

  • Translate product choices into clear requirements covering player flows, game rules, edge cases, tracking needs and acceptance criteria.
  • Coordinate milestones, specialist estimates, capacity and dependencies across Design, Art, Development and QA.
  • Resolve ambiguity and delivery risks early. Negotiate scope, timing and quality trade-offs and escalate decisions outside your authority.

5. Product quality and release management

  • Review technical constraints and product risks with Engineering. Agree release-readiness and quality criteria with Engineering and QA.
  • Coordinate rollout checks and monitoring. During live incidents, clarify player and commercial impact and work through the incident owner on recovery priorities, communication and follow-up.

6. Live operations and publishing

  • Set priorities appropriate to the game lifecycle, balancing new features, content, events and technical health.
  • Review event and content results by player segment and recommend changes based on player response, operating effort and commercial value.
  • Align product readiness with acquisition, store positioning, localization and launch plans. Review acquisition-cohort quality with User Acquisition and manage partner commitments where assigned.

7. Commercial outcomes and accountability

  • Translate business goals into measurable product outcomes with clear baselines and guardrails. Review retention, monetization and relevant cohort economics with Analytics, Finance and User Acquisition.
  • Explain results, investigate material deviations and follow through on corrective actions or investment recommendations. Manage delegated budgets and report product decisions and risks to product or studio leadership.

8. AI adoption and team collaboration

  • Use approved AI tools to improve suitable product workflows, including research support, requirements, localization checks and analysis assistance. Verify outputs and protect company, player and partner information.
  • Measure AI benefits after review and rework. Establish useful review checkpoints and coach junior colleagues in reliable application.
  • Build cross-functional alignment, resolve recurring coordination issues and turn research, experiments and retrospectives into applied learning.

II. QUALIFICATIONS AND CAPABILITIES

Experience and educational background

  • 5–7 years of relevant experience in product management or adjacent game roles, with demonstrated ownership of mobile game features, systems or a product area through delivery and evaluation.
  • A relevant background in product management, game design, business, technology or a related discipline, gained through education or equivalent practical experience.
  • Practical experience using player and commercial evidence to make product decisions. Be prepared to explain your contribution, the trade-offs, the results and what you changed afterward.
  • Global mobile game experience: Experience managing at least one globally released mobile game with 1 million or more cumulative installs is preferred; experience with 5 million or more installs is a strong advantage. Candidates should demonstrate their ownership scope and measurable contribution to product performance.

Knowledge

  • Mobile free-to-play models, player segmentation, core loops, onboarding, progression and difficulty. Understand the economy and advertising or purchase model relevant to the game.
  • Product metrics and cohort economics, including retention, conversion, revenue per active user, lifetime value and acquisition cost, with consistent definitions and time windows.
  • Product discovery, experimentation, game production workflows, requirements and release-quality concepts. Understand enough about technical constraints to work effectively with specialists.
  • AI capabilities and limitations, output verification and responsible handling of confidential data and generated material.

Skills

  • Prioritize roadmaps, build business cases and turn ambiguous problems into clear product requirements and practical plans.
  • Analyze funnels and cohorts, frame hypotheses and interpret experiments with appropriate analytical support. Work confidently with relevant analytics and collaboration tools.
  • Communicate product recommendations clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Negotiate trade-offs and align cross-functional or partner commitments.
  • Coordinate resources, dependencies and risks, and provide useful feedback and coaching to junior colleagues.

Abilities and working approach

  • Exercise independent product judgment within an agreed scope, make proportionate decisions with incomplete information and escalate material risks early.
  • Balance player experience, commercial goals and development constraints, and distinguish evidence from assumptions or misleading metric changes.
  • Take ownership through post-release evaluation, acknowledge failed assumptions and adapt priorities when results or constraints change.
  • Lead through influence, encourage constructive challenge and apply learning consistently to improve the next decision.
  • Language proficiency: Professional working proficiency in Mandarin Chinese and English, both spoken and written, to communicate effectively with development partners and international stakeholders.
  • Platform adaptability: Ability to quickly assess and respond to Google Play and App Store policy and technical changes, coordinating necessary product and release updates with relevant teams while protecting player experience and business performance.

III. EXPECTED DELIVERABLES AND OUTCOMES

You are expected to deliver the following within your assigned product scope:

  • A clear product direction and prioritized roadmap, supported by player needs, commercial reasoning and documented trade-offs.
  • Actionable discovery and experiment results that resolve important uncertainties and lead to explicit continue, change or stop decisions.
  • Clear feature specifications and realistic delivery plans, with visible ownership, dependencies, acceptance criteria and release risks.
  • Measurable progress against agreed player and commercial objectives, supported by reliable data, post-release reviews and timely corrective action.
  • Coordinated releases and lifecycle plans that balance player experience, product quality and operating effort.
  • Reliable AI-assisted workflows and evidence of stronger collaboration or junior capability through applied learning and coaching.
  • Specific targets, baselines, player cohorts, guardrails and review periods will be agreed for the game and its lifecycle stage. Performance will be assessed through the quality of your decisions and execution, as well as the outcomes achieved within your authority and resources.
