jobs.title: Director of FP&A
jobs.excerpt: TL;DRAs Director of FP&A, you'll own the numbers that run Harper: the plan, the forecast, the cash, and the story we tell our board and investors.
jobs.description:
TL;DRAs Director of FP&A, you'll own the numbers that run Harper: the plan, the forecast, the cash, and the story we tell our board and investors. Remote, high ownership, and close to every major decision we make. We are looking for someone who can build a great operating model, partner with department heads as a peer, and walk into a board meeting and explain what the numbers mean, not just what they are. You've built finance functions at venture- or PE-backed software companies, and you're ready to be the strategic finance partner at a company where your work shapes the outcome. If that sounds like you, read on.

Role Overview

The Director of FP&A is Harper's strategic finance lead—the person leadership turns to for a clear view of where the business is, where it's heading, and what it will take to get there. You'll own planning, forecasting, cash, and board reporting, and you'll be a hands-on partner on pricing, partner economics, fundraising, and strategic transactions.

This is a role for someone who is as comfortable in the operating model as in the room with the CEO and the board. You'll build the annual plan with each department head, keep a rolling forecast honest, and turn the data in Salesforce, Xero, Ramp, and Carta into a single source of truth for the metrics that matter—ARR, MRR, NRR, burn, and runway.

You'll also work with our accounting resources to make sure the books are accurate, on time, and audit-ready—without needing to run every journal entry yourself.

We move fast, wear many hats, and value people who flex to get things done. You won't inherit a finance playbook for most things; instead you'll help write it.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Analysis

  • Build the annual operating plan and budget in partnership with each department head, and take it through to board approval.
  • Own the rolling forecast for revenue, expenses, headcount, and cash, plus the runway model.
  • Build scenario models for headcount, pricing, partner terms, and downside cases so leadership can make decisions with eyes open.
  • Forecast revenue from the Salesforce pipeline and the operating model, and own headcount planning and fully loaded cost per role.

What success looks like: Leadership has a plan they trust, a forecast that holds up, and no surprises on cash or runway.

Unit Economics, Pricing & Partner Economics

  • Analyze gross margin by customer and channel, cost to serve, and cloud hosting spend (Linode/Akamai, AWS, GCP).
  • Support the deal desk with pricing and deal economics on enterprise opportunities.
  • Model partner economics for Akamai and new channel partners, and pressure-test proposed terms before we sign.
  • Define our KPIs and maintain one source of truth for metrics (ARR, MRR, NRR, burn, runway) across the company.

What success looks like: Every pricing and partner decision is backed by clear economics, and everyone at Harper uses the same numbers.

Board & Investor Reporting

  • Own the financial section and KPI pages of the board deck, and the board-approved budget.
  • Track financing agreement milestones and conditions, and keep leadership ahead of upcoming obligations.
  • Respond to investor and portfolio requests, including reporting and benchmarking.
  • Provide the financial inputs for quarterly stockholder updates and the weekly leadership summary.

What success looks like: The board and investors get accurate, timely, and insightful reporting, and see finance as a strength of the company.

Equity, Capital & Strategic Transactions

  • Coordinate the cap table with legal and Carta, and own stock-based compensation expense.
  • Lead fundraising support: the model, the data room, and diligence responses.
  • Support strategic transactions with modeling, diligence, and quality-of-earnings preparation.
  • Track convertible notes and debt instruments.

What success looks like: Harper is always diligence-ready, and capital events move quickly because the numbers are already in order.

Systems, Process & Controls

  • Own the finance stack (Xero, Ramp, Salesforce, the operating model, Carta) and how the tools connect.
  • Run the close calendar and the budget calendar.
  • Set approval policies and spend controls, and document finance processes so they scale.

What success looks like: Finance runs on a predictable rhythm, with controls that protect the company without slowing it down.

Success in This Role Looks Like

  • Harper has a board-approved plan and a rolling forecast leadership actually uses to make decisions.
  • Pricing, deal, and partner decisions are grounded in clear unit economics.
  • The board and investors receive accurate, on-time, and insightful reporting.
  • Metrics have one definition and one source of truth across the company.
  • The close is timely and clean, and the company is ready for diligence or audit at any time.

What This Role Is Not

This role is intentionally different from many traditional finance positions. To ensure clarity and alignment, it is important to understand what this role is not:

  • Not a reporting-only role. We need someone who shapes decisions, not just someone who produces the numbers after the fact. You'll have a point of view and share it.
  • Not a hands-on controller role. You'll oversee accounting and the close and be accountable for their quality, but your center of gravity is planning, analysis, and strategic finance.
  • Not a big-company finance seat. There is no large team underneath you and no established playbook. You'll build models, processes, and controls from the ground up.
  • Not a narrowly scoped function. The role spans planning, board reporting, pricing, partner economics, capital, vendors, and systems—comfort across strategic, operational, and interpersonal dimensions is required.

Qualifications

Required

  • Deep FP&A and strategic finance experience (top priority). 8–12+ years in FP&A, strategic finance, or a related finance leadership role, including time at a venture- or PE-backed software company.
  • Board and investor reporting. You've owned the financial section of a board deck and built a board-approved budget.
  • Exceptional modeling skills. You can build an operating model, revenue forecast, cash forecast, and scenario models from scratch—and make them easy for others to use.
  • SaaS and usage-based revenue fluency. You understand ARR, MRR, NRR, gross margin, and cost to serve, including channel and usage-based revenue.
  • Accounting foundation. Strong working knowledge of GAAP, revenue recognition, and the monthly close, with the judgment to oversee accounting work done by others.
  • Capital and transaction experience. Exposure to fundraising, diligence, cap table management, or strategic transactions.
  • Comfort with ambiguity and ownership. You thrive in fast-moving, early-stage environments and hold yourself accountable for outcomes.
  • Excellent communication skills. You can translate the numbers into clear recommendations for department heads, executives, and the board.

Preferred

  • Experience modeling partner or channel economics and supporting a deal desk.
  • Experience with infrastructure, database, or cloud software businesses and their hosting cost structures.
  • Experience implementing or improving finance systems and spend controls at a growing company.
  • CPA, CFA, or MBA.

Nice to Have

  • Hands-on experience with Xero, Ramp, Salesforce, and Carta.
  • Fluency with AI tools to speed up analysis, modeling, and reporting.

Tools We Use

Xero, Ramp, Salesforce, Carta, Google Workspace (Sheets), Slack, Zoom, Microsoft tools.

Why This Role Matters at Harper

The Director of FP&A is how Harper turns ambition into a plan it can execute. This role gives leadership and the board a clear, trusted view of the business, grounds every major decision—pricing, partnerships, hiring, and capital—in sound economics, and makes sure we have the runway to get where we're going. As Harper scales through partnerships and enterprise growth, strong financial leadership is what lets us move fast with confidence.

Salary: $180,000 – $210,000 / year

jobs.description:
Group Head of Project Management Office (PMO) – Insurance & Investments

1. Role Summary

The Group Head of PMO is responsible for leading and overseeing the Group's project management function across all subsidiaries, business units, and geographical markets within the Insurance & Investments sector.

The role establishes group-wide project governance, portfolio management standards, delivery frameworks, and performance monitoring systems to ensure that strategic projects and transformation initiatives are executed effectively. The position provides centralized oversight of project priorities, budgets, resources, risks, dependencies, and expected business outcomes.

Working closely with the Group CEO, executive leadership, subsidiary CEOs, and business heads, the Group Head of PMO ensures that all major projects support the organization's strategic growth, operational efficiency, digital transformation, and long-term business objectives.

2. Key Responsibilities

Group PMO Strategy & Governance

  • Develop and implement the Group's overall Project Management Office strategy, structure, and operating framework.
  • Establish standardized project management methodologies, governance policies, procedures, and reporting requirements across all subsidiaries.
  • Define project approval processes, stage-gate reviews, escalation procedures, and accountability frameworks.
  • Ensure project portfolios are aligned with the Group's strategic objectives and business priorities.
  • Establish consistent project management standards and controls across geographical markets and business units.

Strategic Project Portfolio Management

  • Oversee the consolidated project portfolio across insurance, investment, corporate, and operational business units.
  • Evaluate, prioritize, and monitor strategic projects based on business value, financial impact, risk exposure, and resource requirements.
  • Monitor project progress, milestones, dependencies, budgets, timelines, and deliverables.
  • Identify underperforming projects and recommend corrective actions or changes in resource allocation.
  • Provide executive leadership with a consolidated view of project portfolio performance.

Insurance & Investment Project Oversight

  • Oversee group-wide projects involving insurance product development, underwriting, claims management, policy administration, and distribution expansion.
  • Monitor investment-related projects involving portfolio reporting, investment operations, wealth management platforms, and client servicing, where applicable.
  • Coordinate strategic initiatives involving regulatory compliance, business process modernization, and operational efficiency.
  • Support the implementation of new financial products, business models, and market expansion initiatives.
  • Ensure projects meet relevant insurance, investment, financial services, and corporate governance requirements.

Digital Transformation & Technology Projects

  • Provide governance and oversight for group-wide technology modernization and digital transformation initiatives.
  • Coordinate implementation of enterprise systems, CRM platforms, automation solutions, AI applications, and digital financial services.
  • Work with CIO, CTO, CDO, and business leadership to ensure successful technology project delivery.
  • Monitor system integration, implementation risks, technology budgets, and business adoption.
  • Ensure digital initiatives deliver measurable improvements in customer experience and operational performance.

Financial & Resource Management

  • Oversee consolidated project budgets, financial forecasts, and expenditure tracking across the Group.
  • Monitor project cost performance and identify opportunities for cost optimization.
  • Coordinate resource allocation across subsidiaries, departments, and strategic initiatives.
  • Evaluate project business cases, cost-benefit analysis, ROI, and expected benefits.
  • Ensure effective utilization of internal teams, external consultants, contractors, and implementation partners.

Risk, Compliance & Quality Management

  • Establish group-level project risk management and escalation frameworks.
  • Monitor operational, financial, regulatory, technology, and implementation risks across project portfolios.
  • Coordinate with group risk, compliance, legal, and internal audit functions.
  • Ensure projects comply with internal policies, governance standards, and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Establish contingency and mitigation plans for critical projects and strategic programs.

Performance Reporting & Benefits Realization

  • Develop group-wide project dashboards, performance reports, and executive presentations.
  • Monitor project delivery against approved scope, budgets, timelines, milestones, and quality standards.
  • Track financial benefits, operational improvements, and ROI from strategic initiatives.
  • Prepare regular portfolio performance reports for the Group CEO, Board, and executive committees.
  • Recommend strategic interventions to improve project execution and delivery performance.

Stakeholder & Subsidiary Management

  • Work closely with subsidiary CEOs, managing directors, business unit heads, project sponsors, and program directors.
  • Facilitate group-level project steering committees and portfolio review meetings.
  • Coordinate project planning and delivery across subsidiaries and corporate functions.
  • Manage relationships with external consultants, technology vendors, contractors, and implementation partners.
  • Ensure consistent communication, accountability, and reporting across all Group entities.

Leadership & PMO Capability Development

  • Lead and develop the Group PMO team, including PMO directors, project managers, project analysts, and project controls specialists.
  • Establish PMO structures, responsibilities, and reporting relationships across subsidiaries.
  • Develop project management training, mentoring, and capability-building initiatives.
  • Promote a culture of accountability, transparency, collaboration, and delivery excellence.
  • Drive continuous improvement in project management maturity across the organization.

3. Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Finance, Project Management, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field.
  • MBA or Master's degree in Project Management, Business Strategy, Finance, or a relevant discipline preferred.
  • 12–15+ years of progressive experience in project management, program management, portfolio management, or enterprise transformation.
  • At least 5 years in a senior PMO leadership position overseeing multiple business units, subsidiaries, or large project portfolios.
  • Experience in insurance, reinsurance, banking, investment management, asset management, wealth management, or diversified financial services.
  • Proven track record of establishing or leading enterprise-level or group-level PMO functions.
  • Strong knowledge of project portfolio governance, financial management, resource planning, risk management, and strategic execution.
  • Experience managing complex, multi-country or multi-entity projects and transformation programs.
  • Knowledge of PMI, PRINCE2, Agile, Waterfall, and hybrid project management methodologies.
  • Strong leadership, executive communication, stakeholder management, negotiation, and analytical capabilities.

Preferred Certifications:

- Project Management Professional (PMP).

  • Program Management Professional (PgMP).
  • Portfolio Management Professional (PfMP).

- PRINCE2 Practitioner.

- Agile or Scrum certifications.

4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Percentage of group-wide projects delivered on time and within approved budgets.
  • Overall project portfolio performance against Group strategic objectives.
  • Project cost variance and schedule variance.
  • Group PMO governance and reporting compliance.
  • Successful delivery of strategic insurance and investment initiatives.
  • Project risk identification, mitigation, and escalation effectiveness.
  • Resource utilization and allocation efficiency across subsidiaries.
  • Benefits realization and ROI of major strategic projects.
  • Accuracy and timeliness of consolidated project reporting.
  • Stakeholder satisfaction across Group entities.
  • Improvement in project management maturity across subsidiaries.
  • Reduction in project delays, cost overruns, and implementation risks.

Customer Success Consultant (SME) – Analytical Products


Are you passionate about helping customers turn research data and analytics into meaningful insights and outcomes?

Would you like to combine product expertise with consultative customer engagement to help research institutions maximize the value of Elsevier solutions?


About the Team

The Subject Matter Expert (SME) team is part of Elsevier Customer Success and brings product and domain expertise across Elsevier solutions.

We work closely with Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Sales, SEMs, Product, Support, and Customer Education to address complex customer needs, strengthen adoption and value realization, and support key customer accounts.

The team also brings customer and market insights back into the business, helping us continuously improve our products, services, and overall customer experience.


About the Role

As a Customer Success Consultant (SME) – Analytical Products, you will provide product and domain expertise, consultative support, and institution-level advisory services to Elsevier customers throughout their post-sales journey.

You will work closely with Customer Success Managers, Sales, and other internal teams to help customers address complex needs, successfully adopt Elsevier solutions into their institutional workflows, and achieve meaningful research and business outcomes.

You will proactively engage where specialist expertise can increase customer value, address adoption gaps, support strategic use cases, or help mitigate customer risk.

The role combines strong product knowledge with an understanding of research analytics, research evaluation, bibliometrics, and the broader scholarly research and publishing ecosystem.

As a Customer Success Consultant (SME) – Analytical Products, you will:

  • Partner with Customer Success Managers, Sales, SEMs, and regional teams to identify customers who would benefit from specialist support.
  • Provide consultative support to help customers understand their priorities, interpret research data and indicators, and apply Elsevier solutions within their institutional workflows.
  • Support the adoption and advanced use of analytical products such as SciVal and Scopus.
  • Act as a trusted advisor, helping translate customer needs into practical use cases, recommendations, and measurable outcomes.
  • Provide advanced product guidance, consultation, and training and assist with complex customer needs or escalations.
  • Contribute to long-term customer engagement, value realization, retention, renewal, and account growth.
  • Maintain knowledge of Elsevier analytical and AI capabilities, Generative AI developments, research evaluation, and the scholarly publishing ecosystem.
  • Work across Product, Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Support, and Customer Education to share customer feedback and market insights.
  • Identify recurring customer needs, market trends, and adoption barriers to support improvements in our products and customer experience.
  • Maintain visibility of customer priorities, SME activities, and outcomes through agreed systems such as Gainsight.

Requirements

To be successful as a Customer Success Consultant (SME) – Analytical Products, you will:

  • Have experience or knowledge in research analytics, scholarly publishing, information science, data analysis, or a related area.

We promote a healthy work/life balance across the organisation. We offer an appealing working prospect for our people. With numerous wellbeing initiatives, shared parental leave, study assistance and sabbaticals, we will help you meet your immediate responsibilities and your long-term goals.

At Elsevier, your work contributes to the world's grand challenges and a more sustainable future. We harness innovative technologies to support science and healthcare to partner for a better world.

1. Role Summary

The Director of Project Management Office (PMO) is responsible for establishing, leading, and managing the organization's Project Management Office to ensure effective governance, planning, execution, monitoring, and delivery of strategic and operational projects.

The role oversees the project portfolio across insurance, investment, corporate operations, technology, digital transformation, and business development functions. The Director of PMO ensures projects are delivered within approved timelines, budgets, quality standards, and organizational objectives while maintaining effective risk management, resource allocation, and stakeholder engagement.

The successful candidate will drive project management excellence, strengthen governance frameworks, improve delivery performance, and ensure that project outcomes contribute to business growth, operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and customer experience.

A. PMO Strategy, Leadership & Governance

  • Establish, develop, and lead the organization's Project Management Office.
  • Define PMO strategy, policies, methodologies, standards, and governance frameworks.
  • Implement standardized project management processes, tools, templates, and reporting structures.
  • Establish project approval processes, stage gates, escalation procedures, and accountability frameworks.
  • Promote project management best practices across departments and business units.
  • Ensure alignment between project execution and corporate strategy.

  • Monitor project progress and identify delays, delivery challenges, and performance gaps.

  • Recommend improvements to project delivery processes and organizational performance.

  • Facilitate communication and coordination across business units and functional teams.

You are the person who keeps the plan. When 6 people are talking at once on a customer call about data files, go-live dates and who owns what, you are already typing the action items, assigning owners and setting due dates. By the time the call ends, your recap is ready to send.

  • An air traffic controller: you run a 200-task Asana plan across several customers and always know what is landing next.
  • A live capture pro: you think while you type, and you organize as you go. Notes land in the right place the first time.
  • One step ahead: like a great surgical tech who hands over the next instrument before anyone asks, you anticipate what the team and the customer will need next.
  • Unafraid of complexity: Medicare, Medicaid, SFTP, eligibility files. When you hear a term you do not know, you ask, learn it and use it correctly the next time.
  • Warm and professional: you welcome customers to a call, deliver hard news with calm and kindness, and guide people through change.
  • Here to master the craft: you love this kind of work and want to grow in it.

What You Will Do

Run the plan

  • Build project plans that work backward from customer goals, tracking every deliverable, owner and deadline.
  • Capture decisions and next steps in real time in Asana and Salesforce (for example, "Per 6/15 discussion, Sunbelt will pilot new workflows by Q3").
  • Act as the hub between internal teams (Product, Tech, Workforce Development, Clinical) and hold everyone to the timeline.

See around corners

  • Spot risks early and flag them before they become blockers.
  • Know what to solve on your own and when to escalate.
  • Prepare customers for delays and tradeoffs before they become surprises.

Deliver for customers

  • Partner with a Director of Clinical Strategy to support 4-12 healthcare customers, depending on complexity.
  • Coordinate end-to-end Community Health Worker program launches and platform adoption.
  • Prepare agendas, decks and quarterly business reviews, and pull customer reports.
  • Own the Tech Review process with customer IT and compliance teams.
  • Triage a steady flow of email, Slack and customer requests so nothing is missed.

What You Bring

  • Required: a Bachelor's degree and a project management certification (PMP or CAPM).
  • 2+ years managing complex projects, implementations, or operations with external customers or partners.
  • A track record of managing concurrent projects with zero dropped balls.
  • The ability to turn a long discussion into a 1-page summary executives love.
  • Hands-on skill with Asana or a similar tool, the Google suite, Zoom and a CRM such as Salesforce.
  • Ability to work primarily during Eastern Time business hours.
  • Occasional travel for team retreats and customer site visits.

Nice to have: familiarity with U.S. healthcare (health systems, payers, community-based organizations) or experience at a health tech or SaaS startup.

Our Hiring Process

Live note-taking is central to this role, so we test it early. After you apply and answer a few short questions, selected candidates complete a short live note-taking exercise and a screening interview, followed by a project plan exercise and team interviews.

IMPaCT Care is committed to providing an inclusive interview experience. If you need any accommodations to participate fully, please let us know.

One of our core values is to create a diverse workplace that welcomes and values each team member's unique perspective, background and ideas. We are committed to an inclusive and diverse workplace.

Job Description: Director of PMO – Insurance & Investments

1. Role Summary

The Director of Project Management Office (PMO) is responsible for establishing, leading, and managing the organization's Project Management Office to ensure effective governance, planning, execution, monitoring, and delivery of strategic and operational projects.

The role oversees the project portfolio across insurance, investment, corporate operations, technology, digital transformation, and business development functions. The Director of PMO ensures projects are delivered within approved timelines, budgets, quality standards, and organizational objectives while maintaining effective risk management, resource allocation, and stakeholder engagement.

The successful candidate will drive project management excellence, strengthen governance frameworks, improve delivery performance, and ensure that project outcomes contribute to business growth, operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and customer experience.

2. Key Responsibilities

A. PMO Strategy, Leadership & Governance

  • Establish, develop, and lead the organization's Project Management Office.
  • Define PMO strategy, policies, methodologies, standards, and governance frameworks.
  • Implement standardized project management processes, tools, templates, and reporting structures.
  • Establish project approval processes, stage gates, escalation procedures, and accountability frameworks.
  • Promote project management best practices across departments and business units.
  • Ensure alignment between project execution and corporate strategy.

B. Project Portfolio Management

  • Oversee the organization's project portfolio, ensuring alignment with strategic priorities.
  • Evaluate project proposals, business cases, feasibility studies, and investment requirements.
  • Prioritize projects based on business value, financial impact, risk, and resource availability.
  • Monitor project dependencies, interdepartmental coordination, and portfolio-level risks.
  • Provide recommendations to senior management regarding project prioritization and resource allocation.
  • Track portfolio performance and ensure delivery of expected business benefits.

C. Project Planning & Execution

  • Oversee the planning, scheduling, budgeting, and execution of strategic projects.
  • Ensure project managers develop comprehensive project plans, milestones, deliverables, and resource requirements.
  • Monitor project progress and identify delays, delivery challenges, and performance gaps.
  • Drive corrective actions and escalation processes to maintain project delivery commitments.
  • Ensure projects are completed within approved scope, budget, timelines, and quality standards.
  • Coordinate cross-functional teams to ensure smooth project implementation.

D. Insurance & Investment Project Oversight

  • Oversee projects related to insurance operations, underwriting, claims management, policy administration, and distribution.
  • Coordinate initiatives involving investment operations, financial products, portfolio reporting, and client services, where applicable.
  • Support the implementation of regulatory, compliance, risk management, and internal control initiatives.
  • Monitor projects involving new product development, market expansion, operational improvements, and business integration.
  • Ensure project deliverables reflect the operational and regulatory requirements of the insurance and financial services industry.

E. Digital Transformation & Technology Projects

  • Oversee technology-enabled transformation projects, including core insurance systems, CRM, ERP, digital platforms, and automation initiatives.
  • Coordinate with IT, technology, operations, and business teams to ensure successful implementation.
  • Monitor technology project budgets, vendor performance, implementation timelines, and delivery quality.
  • Support digitalization, process automation, data management, and operational efficiency initiatives.
  • Ensure technology projects deliver measurable business outcomes.

F. Financial & Resource Management

  • Develop and monitor project budgets, financial forecasts, and expenditure reports.
  • Ensure effective allocation and utilization of project resources.
  • Monitor project costs, financial variances, and budget performance.
  • Evaluate project financial risks and recommend cost-control measures.
  • Coordinate with Finance and Procurement teams on project funding, contracts, and vendor payments.
  • Assess project return on investment (ROI) and benefits realization.

G. Risk Management, Compliance & Quality Assurance

  • Establish project risk management frameworks and escalation mechanisms.
  • Identify, assess, and monitor project risks, issues, dependencies, and delivery constraints.
  • Ensure projects comply with applicable regulatory requirements, internal policies, and governance standards.
  • Monitor project quality and ensure deliverables meet agreed specifications.
  • Maintain project documentation, audit trails, and management records.
  • Coordinate with Risk, Compliance, Legal, and Internal Audit teams.

H. Performance Monitoring & Executive Reporting

  • Develop project dashboards, management reports, and portfolio performance metrics.
  • Present project status, risks, budget performance, and delivery updates to executive leadership.
  • Provide timely visibility into project delays, resource constraints, and critical dependencies.
  • Monitor project KPIs and ensure accountability among project managers.
  • Lead project review meetings and portfolio governance sessions.
  • Recommend improvements to project delivery processes and organizational performance.

I. Stakeholder & Team Management

  • Lead and develop project managers, PMO analysts, and project support professionals.
  • Build strong working relationships with senior executives, department heads, project sponsors, and external vendors.
  • Facilitate communication and coordination across business units and functional teams.
  • Develop project management capabilities through training, coaching, and performance management.
  • Promote a culture of ownership, collaboration, transparency, and continuous improvement.

3. Required Qualifications & Experience

Educational Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Project Management, Finance, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field.
  • Master's degree in Business Administration (MBA), Project Management, Finance, or a relevant discipline is preferred.

Professional Experience

  • Minimum 10–15 years of progressive professional experience in project management, program management, or portfolio management.
  • At least 5 years in a senior PMO leadership or Director-level position.
  • Proven experience establishing, managing, or transforming a Project Management Office.
  • Experience overseeing complex, enterprise-wide projects and cross-functional initiatives.
  • Background in insurance, banking, financial services, investment management, or related industries is highly desirable.
  • Experience managing large project portfolios, budgets, resources, and multiple project teams.
  • Exposure to digital transformation, technology implementation, business process improvement, and organizational change initiatives.

Preferred Certifications

- Project Management Professional (PMP).

- PRINCE2 Practitioner.

- Managing Successful Programmes (MSP).

  • Portfolio Management Professional (PfMP).

- Agile or Scrum certifications.

- Lean Six Sigma certification.

Core Competencies

  • Strategic project and portfolio management.
  • PMO governance and operational leadership.
  • Financial planning and budget management.

- Risk assessment and problem-solving.

  • Executive communication and stakeholder management.
  • Change management and business transformation.
  • Leadership, team development, and decision-making.
  • Project management systems and reporting tools.

4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Percentage of projects delivered on time and within approved budgets.
  • Overall project portfolio performance and delivery success rate.

- Project cost and schedule variance.

  • Achievement of project milestones and strategic objectives.

- Project benefits realization and ROI.

  • Effectiveness of project governance and reporting.
  • Project risk identification, mitigation, and resolution.
  • Resource utilization and allocation efficiency.
  • Stakeholder satisfaction and project sponsor feedback.
  • PMO process maturity and continuous improvement.
  • Compliance with project management standards and regulatory requirements.

Our Story
Imagine being part of a team that’s not just shaping the future but actively driving it. The Claim Counsel / Senior Complex Representative manages high-severity and technically complex claims across healthcare and specialty professional liability programs. Coverage Analysis

  • For extra-contractual claims, evaluate underlying claim-handling facts, settlement opportunities, communications, damages, and applicable legal standards without prejudging coverage or liability.
  • Develop, document, and execute claim strategies, action plans, and litigation management plans tailored to the applicable program and carrier requirements.

Preferred

jobs.title: Senior Program Delivery Professional, Benefit Enablement & Execution
jobs.excerpt: Become a part of our caring community Humana’s Consumer Product Management team is looking for an experienced Senior Program Delivery Professional, Benefit Enablement & Execution, to join working remote anywhere in the US.
jobs.description:
Become a part of our caring community

Humana’s Consumer Product Management team is looking for an experienced Senior Program Delivery Professional, Benefit Enablement & Execution, to join working remote anywhere in the US. In this role, you'll work closely with Product Managers and cross-functional partners to move bid initiatives, research and process work from idea through delivery. You'll coordinate the analysis behind benefit and portfolio decisions, maintain accurate documentation and milestone plans, and support teams as they adopt new processes and tools. If you enjoy connecting strategy to execution and making sure deliverables stay on track, this role is for you.

As Senior Program Delivery Professional, Benefit Enablement & Execution, you'll help translate Medicare Advantage portfolio priorities into accurate analysis, well-defined deliverables and coordinated execution. Working closely with Lead Product Managers and cross-functional partners, you'll move bid initiatives, research and process improvements from concept through implementation while keeping decisions, documentation and milestones aligned.

You'll perform the detailed product, benefit, market, operational and regulatory analysis that informs portfolio direction. You'll coordinate feasibility reviews, research enterprise priorities and represent Product Management on assigned cross-functional workgroups. Your work will help leaders understand options, evaluate implications and make informed decisions.

You'll also strengthen the way Product Management operates by maintaining portfolio-governance records, supporting the Process Activation Calendar, improving process documentation, developing training materials and helping implement technology-enabled solutions. You'll take ownership of defined workstreams, identify risks early and build the capability to lead increasingly complex initiatives. This is a highly collaborative individual-contributor role for someone who combines analytical rigor, attention to detail and reliable follow-through with the curiosity and judgment needed to operate effectively in a fast-moving Medicare Advantage environment.


Key Role Functions


Support Medicare Advantage Bid Initiatives

  • Partner with Lead Product Managers, Growth and Strategy, and functional teams to support bid initiatives involving benefit standardization, portfolio segmentation, product guiding principles and other portfolio priorities
  • Translate initiative objectives into defined analyses, deliverables, milestones and follow-up actions for assigned workstreams
  • Gather, validate and compare benefit, market, portfolio and operational information to inform recommendations and decisions
  • Prepare analyses that identify patterns, differences, risks, assumptions and potential member or portfolio impacts
  • Coordinate inputs from subject-matter experts and ensure required information is complete, accurate and delivered on time
  • Maintain initiative documentation and provide clear progress updates, open questions and recommended next steps
  • Apply lessons learned from each cycle to improve future analyses, templates and delivery practices

Coordinate Feasibility Reviews and Decision Support

  • Coordinate structured reviews of proposed benefits and product opportunities across product, operations, compliance, clinical, technology, systems and other relevant functions
  • Define and communicate the information, questions, owners and timelines needed to complete assigned feasibility assessments
  • Collect and organize partner input, identify conflicting information and follow up on unresolved questions
  • Distinguish confirmed requirements from assumptions and areas requiring further validation
  • Summarize feasibility findings, dependencies, constraints and execution considerations in clear decision-support materials
  • Escalate material gaps, risks or timing concerns to Lead Product Managers or the Program Delivery team early enough to support resolution
  • Document recommendations, decisions, rationale, owners and follow-up actions

Conduct Enterprise Research and Product Impact Analysis

  • Research Stars, Clinical, Regulatory Compliance, the Complaints Tracking Module and other enterprise initiatives affecting Medicare Advantage products
  • Gather information from relevant business, regulatory and functional sources and assess its reliability and applicability
  • Identify potential impacts to benefit design, product processes, portfolio priorities, systems, operations and the member experience
  • Synthesize complex findings into concise briefs, presentations, recommendations and decision points for Product Management and partner leaders
  • Represent Product Management on assigned cross-functional workgroups and accurately communicate Product requirements and considerations
  • Track commitments, decisions and follow-up actions and ensure the appropriate Product Management partners remain informed
  • Escalate issues requiring broader product direction, functional expertise or leadership decisions

Support the Process Activation Calendar

  • Work with functional partners to confirm milestone dates, dependencies, accountable owners and completion requirements for assigned bid and product activities
  • Add approved milestones and updates to the Process Activation Calendar accurately and within established timelines
  • Communicate calendar changes to affected teams and clarify required actions or handoffs
  • Monitor milestone progress, follow up with owners and maintain current completion status and supporting information
  • Identify missed, conflicting or at-risk milestones and assess potential downstream impacts
  • Escalate material risks to Lead Product Managers or the Program Delivery team with clear facts, impacts and recommended next steps
  • Use milestone results and lessons learned to improve future calendar planning and follow-up practices

Improve Processes, Tools and Ways of Working

  • Partner with Process Improvement and Program Delivery, Product Management and functional teams to draft, maintain and improve process documentation, templates and workflows
  • Document processes in a clear, practical format that defines activities, ownership, handoffs, controls and expected outcomes
  • Identify manual, repetitive or error-prone work that could be simplified, standardized or automated
  • Help evaluate, test and implement approved technology solutions using tools such as Power Automate, Power BI, Copilot, SharePoint and related platforms
  • Complete user-acceptance testing, document issues and confirm that solutions meet defined business needs before broader rollout
  • Monitor adoption and gather feedback to identify needed refinements
  • Maintain appropriate documentation and controls so process and technology improvements are sustainable

Develop Training and Product Management Capability

  • Develop job aids, quick-reference guides, process walkthroughs, presentations and other training materials as tools, processes and requirements change
  • Translate complex requirements into clear instructions, examples and practical guidance for Product Managers and partner teams
  • Help deliver live training, working sessions and office hours and respond to process questions within the role’s area of expertise
  • Validate training content with process owners and subject-matter experts before distribution
  • Gather participant feedback and update materials when additional clarity or reinforcement is needed
  • Share knowledge, effective practices and lessons learned across the Product Management team
  • Build expertise and judgment by progressing from supporting initiatives to independently leading defined workstreams


Use your skills to make an impact

Required Qualifications

  • 4+ years of relevant health plan, product management, or program delivery experience
  • Experience conducting research and analysis and translating findings into clear recommendations or decision-support materials
  • Experience coordinating deliverables, milestones or workstreams across multiple partners
  • Demonstrated ability to organize complex information, maintain accurate documentation and manage competing priorities
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify patterns, gaps, risks and unresolved questions
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to tailor information for working teams and leaders
  • Demonstrated ability to influence follow-through and maintain accountability without formal authority
  • Advanced proficiency with Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Teams and related digital collaboration tools

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher
  • Medicare Advantage product management, bid, implementation or operational experience
  • Experience with benefit design, benefit comparison, service-area expansion or plan naming
  • Knowledge of CMS Medicare Advantage requirements, bid processes, PBP or HPMS
  • Knowledge of Stars, the Complaints Tracking Module, member experience or regulatory compliance programs
  • Experience supporting feasibility reviews across regulatory, operational, system, clinical or financial considerations
  • Experience maintaining program-governance materials, milestone calendars, decision logs or dashboards
  • Experience writing process documentation, job aids, quick-reference guides or training materials
  • Experience facilitating workgroups, training sessions or process walkthroughs
  • Experience using Power Automate, Power BI, Copilot or similar tools to improve processes, reporting or administrative efficiency
  • Process improvement experience or training, including Lean, Six Sigma or another structured improvement methodology

Additional Information

  • This role typically operates on Eastern Standard Time business hours.
  • The work follows the annual Medicare Advantage and CMS regulatory cycle. Certain periods of the year require additional flexibility, including extended hours and occasional weekend work, to meet critical regulatory and business deadlines.

What Success Looks Like

  • Deliver accurate, timely work. Meet or exceed expectations for quality, completeness and timeliness across analysis, documentation, training and milestone deliverables
  • Turn data into insight. Gather, validate, compare and interpret benefit, market, portfolio and operational information and explain what it means for the business and members
  • Make complex topics understandable. Translate Stars, Clinical, CTM, regulatory and enterprise topics into clear takeaways, implications and recommended actions
  • Communicate with purpose. Know what to communicate, when, to whom and at what level of detail in a matrixed organization
  • Own the details. Keep governance records, decisions, requirements and calendars accurate, current and easy to use
  • Follow through. Track commitments, engage owners and drive assigned deliverables to completion, including with partners you do not manage
  • Raise risks early. Identify gaps, dependencies and at-risk milestones before they create downstream impacts and escalate them with useful context
  • Manage competing priorities. Organize multiple workstreams, adjust quickly as needs change and maintain quality under compressed timelines
  • Improve how work gets done. Identify practical opportunities to simplify processes, strengthen controls and replace manual work with technology-enabled solutions
  • Help others succeed. Explain processes and tools clearly and create training that supports consistent adoption
  • Grow ownership and judgment. Progress from supporting initiatives to independently leading defined analyses and workstreams
  • Keep the member in view. Consider how analysis, process and delivery decisions affect the clarity, reliability and value of the member experience

How You'll Lead

How you achieve results matters as much as what you deliver. You'll model Humana's values by being Caring, Curious and Committed, and you'll put the Humana Way into practice by living the Golden Rule, keeping work simple, playing to win, keeping your eyes on the horizon and playing as one team.


You'll listen before assuming, ask thoughtful questions and remain open to learning. You'll turn details into useful insights, simplify processes where possible and focus on outcomes rather than activity alone. You'll establish clear endpoints for assigned work, anticipate dependencies and adjust as conditions change. You'll seek diverse perspectives, communicate openly and build trust by following through on commitments to customers, teammates and the business.


Role Expectations

  • Operate independently on assigned analyses, deliverables and workstreams within established Product Management, Medicare Advantage, regulatory and enterprise strategies
  • Apply broad product, process and business knowledge to resolve varied and moderately complex issues
  • Determine the appropriate analytical approach, work sequence and stakeholder engagement needed to complete assigned work
  • Exercise judgment in evaluating information, identifying risks and recommending next steps while recognizing when decisions must be elevated
  • Influence outcomes through credible analysis, clear communication and reliable follow-through rather than formal authority
  • Coordinate cross-functional contributors and maintain accountability for assigned deliverables and milestones
  • Manage several concurrent priorities with differing timelines, stakeholders and dependencies
  • Communicate findings and recommendations in formats appropriate for working teams and leaders
  • Contribute to functional improvements by identifying recurring issues and recommending practical process, documentation or technology changes
  • Use advanced digital tools, including Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Teams and approved automation or reporting platforms, to analyze information, manage work and communicate effectively
  • Adapt quickly as priorities, requirements and business conditions change.
  • Demonstrate readiness for increasing ownership by independently leading defined portions of broader initiatives

Key Partnerships & Reporting Relationship

You'll report to the Director, Insurance Product Management and work closely with Lead Product Managers. You'll also partner with Growth and Strategy, Process Improvement and Program Delivery, Stars, Clinical, Compliance, Operations, Marketing, Technology and other Product Management and enterprise teams.

This role does not have direct people-management responsibility; however, you'll contribute through cross-functional influence and program ownership.

Work at Home Requirements: To ensure Home or Hybrid Home/Office employees’ ability to work effectively, the self-provided internet service of Home or Hybrid Home/Office employees must meet the following criteria: At minimum, a download speed of 25 Mbps and an upload speed of 10 Mbps is required; wireless, wired cable or DSL connection is suggested. In certain roles, the minimum recommended internet speed required by Humana may not be sufficient for business needs. Humana reserves the right to require associates to upgrade their internet service if necessary. Work from a dedicated space lacking ongoing interruptions to protect member PHI / HIPAA information.Travel: While this is a remote position, occasional travel to Humana's offices for training or meetings may be required.

Scheduled Weekly Hours

40

The compensation range below reflects a good faith estimate of starting base pay for full time (40 hours per week) employment at the time of posting. The pay range may be higher or lower based on geographic location and individual pay will vary based on demonstrated job related skills, knowledge, experience, education, certifications, etc.$86,300 - $118,700 per yearThis job is eligible for a bonus incentive plan. This incentive opportunity is based upon company and/or individual performance.

Description of Benefits

Humana, Inc. and its affiliated subsidiaries (collectively, “Humana”) offers competitive benefits that support whole-person well-being. Associate benefits are designed to encourage personal wellness and smart healthcare decisions for you and your family while also knowing your life extends outside of work. Among our benefits, Humana provides medical, dental and vision benefits, 401(k) retirement savings plan, time off (including paid time off, company and personal holidays, paid parental and caregiver leave), short-term and long-term disability, life insurance and many other opportunities.Application Deadline: 11-11-2026


About us

About Humana: Humana Inc. (NYSE: HUM) is a leading U.S. healthcare company. Through our Humana insurance services and our CenterWell healthcare services, we make it easier for the millions of people we serve to achieve their best health – delivering the care and service they need, when they need it. These efforts are leading to a better quality of life for people with Medicare and Medicaid, families, individuals, military service personnel, and communities at large. Learn more about what we offer at Humana.com and at CenterWell.com.

​

Equal Opportunity Employer

About the Team/Role

The incumbent Credit Analyst is expected provide quality credit and financial analysis and recommendations to support the success WEX Bank’s Commercial Credit Risk function and the bank in general. The Analyst will possess an advanced knowledge of all facets of Commercial Credit Risk analysis and under-writing of medium, and large size commercial credit applications in accordance to industry best practices, established bank policies, procedures, laws and regulations. The Analyst will be expected to effectively communicate verbally and in writing with bank leadership, sales representatives, and customers regarding credit decisions and recommendations. The Credit Analyst must be comfortable making complex decisions with limited information and presenting difficult information to customers.


How you'll make an impact

Underwriting:

  • Perform advanced financial / risk analysis for commercial credit lending on our existing customer portfolio with credit limits >$150K
  • Utilize commercial credit reports and other third party data to make credit decisions relative to credit applications in accordance with approved credit policy and established procedures
  • Approve/decline credit requests within personal credit authority

Credit Reviews:

  • Perform financial / credit risk analysis of public and large private companies based upon risk alerts or credit review schedules
  • Utilize intermediate to advanced credit risk analysis methodologies to make complex credit decisions related to account credit line increases, decrease, or loss mitigation strategies
  • Determines the credit worthiness of all accounts not scored by models, and makes those decisions based on broad-based knowledge of practices and industry standards
  • Prepare and present complete and accurate credit packages for management and the Bank Loan Committee recommending and supporting credit decisions
  • Recommend improvements to strategy, policy and procedures

Customer Service & Other

  • Resolve complex credit problems with internal/external customers
  • Assist and respond to customers with requests, questions and complaints regarding their accounts via both email and client meetings.
  • Communicate with customers, relationship managers, and/or bank reference to gather required information

Experience you'll bring

  • Credit Business Associate (CBA) or Credit Business Fellow (CBF) accreditation from NACM preferred or similar industry standard Commercial Credit Lending Certification (i.e. Moody’s CICC) preferred.
  • Advanced level of expertise in understanding/interpreting various financial statement types.

Job Description: Director of PMO – Insurance & Investments

1. Role Summary

The Director of Project Management Office (PMO) is responsible for establishing, leading, and managing the organization's Project Management Office to ensure effective governance, planning, execution, monitoring, and delivery of strategic and operational projects.

The role oversees the project portfolio across insurance, investment, corporate operations, technology, digital transformation, and business development functions. The Director of PMO ensures projects are delivered within approved timelines, budgets, quality standards, and organizational objectives while maintaining effective risk management, resource allocation, and stakeholder engagement.

The successful candidate will drive project management excellence, strengthen governance frameworks, improve delivery performance, and ensure that project outcomes contribute to business growth, operational efficiency, regulatory compliance, and customer experience.

2. Key Responsibilities

A. PMO Strategy, Leadership & Governance

  • Establish, develop, and lead the organization's Project Management Office.
  • Define PMO strategy, policies, methodologies, standards, and governance frameworks.
  • Implement standardized project management processes, tools, templates, and reporting structures.
  • Establish project approval processes, stage gates, escalation procedures, and accountability frameworks.
  • Promote project management best practices across departments and business units.
  • Ensure alignment between project execution and corporate strategy.

B. Project Portfolio Management

  • Oversee the organization's project portfolio, ensuring alignment with strategic priorities.
  • Evaluate project proposals, business cases, feasibility studies, and investment requirements.
  • Prioritize projects based on business value, financial impact, risk, and resource availability.
  • Monitor project dependencies, interdepartmental coordination, and portfolio-level risks.
  • Provide recommendations to senior management regarding project prioritization and resource allocation.
  • Track portfolio performance and ensure delivery of expected business benefits.

C. Project Planning & Execution

  • Oversee the planning, scheduling, budgeting, and execution of strategic projects.
  • Ensure project managers develop comprehensive project plans, milestones, deliverables, and resource requirements.
  • Monitor project progress and identify delays, delivery challenges, and performance gaps.
  • Drive corrective actions and escalation processes to maintain project delivery commitments.
  • Ensure projects are completed within approved scope, budget, timelines, and quality standards.
  • Coordinate cross-functional teams to ensure smooth project implementation.

D. Insurance & Investment Project Oversight

  • Oversee projects related to insurance operations, underwriting, claims management, policy administration, and distribution.
  • Coordinate initiatives involving investment operations, financial products, portfolio reporting, and client services, where applicable.
  • Support the implementation of regulatory, compliance, risk management, and internal control initiatives.
  • Monitor projects involving new product development, market expansion, operational improvements, and business integration.
  • Ensure project deliverables reflect the operational and regulatory requirements of the insurance and financial services industry.

E. Digital Transformation & Technology Projects

  • Oversee technology-enabled transformation projects, including core insurance systems, CRM, ERP, digital platforms, and automation initiatives.
  • Coordinate with IT, technology, operations, and business teams to ensure successful implementation.
  • Monitor technology project budgets, vendor performance, implementation timelines, and delivery quality.
  • Support digitalization, process automation, data management, and operational efficiency initiatives.
  • Ensure technology projects deliver measurable business outcomes.

F. Financial & Resource Management

  • Develop and monitor project budgets, financial forecasts, and expenditure reports.
  • Ensure effective allocation and utilization of project resources.
  • Monitor project costs, financial variances, and budget performance.
  • Evaluate project financial risks and recommend cost-control measures.
  • Coordinate with Finance and Procurement teams on project funding, contracts, and vendor payments.
  • Assess project return on investment (ROI) and benefits realization.

G. Risk Management, Compliance & Quality Assurance

  • Establish project risk management frameworks and escalation mechanisms.
  • Identify, assess, and monitor project risks, issues, dependencies, and delivery constraints.
  • Ensure projects comply with applicable regulatory requirements, internal policies, and governance standards.
  • Monitor project quality and ensure deliverables meet agreed specifications.
  • Maintain project documentation, audit trails, and management records.
  • Coordinate with Risk, Compliance, Legal, and Internal Audit teams.

H. Performance Monitoring & Executive Reporting

  • Develop project dashboards, management reports, and portfolio performance metrics.
  • Present project status, risks, budget performance, and delivery updates to executive leadership.
  • Provide timely visibility into project delays, resource constraints, and critical dependencies.
  • Monitor project KPIs and ensure accountability among project managers.
  • Lead project review meetings and portfolio governance sessions.
  • Recommend improvements to project delivery processes and organizational performance.

I. Stakeholder & Team Management

  • Lead and develop project managers, PMO analysts, and project support professionals.
  • Build strong working relationships with senior executives, department heads, project sponsors, and external vendors.
  • Facilitate communication and coordination across business units and functional teams.
  • Develop project management capabilities through training, coaching, and performance management.
  • Promote a culture of ownership, collaboration, transparency, and continuous improvement.

3. Required Qualifications & Experience

Educational Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Project Management, Finance, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field.
  • Master's degree in Business Administration (MBA), Project Management, Finance, or a relevant discipline is preferred.

Professional Experience

  • Minimum 10–15 years of progressive professional experience in project management, program management, or portfolio management.
  • At least 5 years in a senior PMO leadership or Director-level position.
  • Proven experience establishing, managing, or transforming a Project Management Office.
  • Experience overseeing complex, enterprise-wide projects and cross-functional initiatives.
  • Background in insurance, banking, financial services, investment management, or related industries is highly desirable.
  • Experience managing large project portfolios, budgets, resources, and multiple project teams.
  • Exposure to digital transformation, technology implementation, business process improvement, and organizational change initiatives.

Preferred Certifications

- Project Management Professional (PMP).

- PRINCE2 Practitioner.

- Managing Successful Programmes (MSP).

  • Portfolio Management Professional (PfMP).

- Agile or Scrum certifications.

- Lean Six Sigma certification.

Core Competencies

  • Strategic project and portfolio management.
  • PMO governance and operational leadership.
  • Financial planning and budget management.

- Risk assessment and problem-solving.

  • Executive communication and stakeholder management.
  • Change management and business transformation.
  • Leadership, team development, and decision-making.
  • Project management systems and reporting tools.

4. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Percentage of projects delivered on time and within approved budgets.
  • Overall project portfolio performance and delivery success rate.

- Project cost and schedule variance.

  • Achievement of project milestones and strategic objectives.

- Project benefits realization and ROI.

  • Effectiveness of project governance and reporting.
  • Project risk identification, mitigation, and resolution.
  • Resource utilization and allocation efficiency.
  • Stakeholder satisfaction and project sponsor feedback.
  • PMO process maturity and continuous improvement.
  • Compliance with project management standards and regulatory requirements.

jobs.title: Head of Business Development, Inference Service Providers & AI Cloud Offtake
jobs.excerpt: As Head of Business Development at vCluster Labs, you aren’t just brokering GPU deals; you are building vCluster’s global offtake business from the first match.
jobs.description:
As Head of Business Development at vCluster Labs, you aren’t just brokering GPU deals; you are building vCluster’s global offtake business from the first match. You pair inference service providers (ISPs) with AI Clouds, secure the buyer’s minimum purchase commitment for an agreed term, and stay through the first paid workload. When an operator needs vCluster for tenant isolation or vMetal to provision bare-metal GPUs, you win the software order with Sales.

As Head of Business Development, your role will include:

  • Global GPU supply: You will lead commercial relationships with participating NVIDIA Cloud Partners (NCPs) and other AI Clouds. You will verify technical readiness and reservation authority at onboarding, then track available, reserved, and planned capacity weekly by GPU type, count, region, price, and delivery date.

  • Funded inference demand: You will reach ISPs, model builders, AI startups, and ISVs directly and through developer communities, with NVIDIA Inception referrals where relevant. You will verify the budget owner, launch date, and minimum commitment before a buyer enters the funnel.

  • vCluster’s matchmaking system: With RevOps and Product, you will launch the workflow for intake, routing, and partner acceptance. You will match buyers on performance, residency, price, and timing, give each referral an owner and response date, and reroute opportunities that stall.

  • Partner enablement and co-sell: You will create partner-specific offers, sales playbooks, and technical workshops with Marketing and developer relations. You will run joint campaigns, co-sell with partner reps and vCluster Sales, and measure which trials convert to paid production.

  • Demand forecasting and capacity guidance: You will forecast usage by GPU type, region, and month from buyer ramp plans, pipeline, and actual consumption, counting each workload once across bids. You will show signed commitments and upside separately, and advise AI Cloud executives where to add, reallocate, or defer GPUs.

  • Offtake through first billing and vCluster revenue: You will validate performance with Solutions Engineering and lead buyer and provider negotiations on price, minimums, ramp schedules, service levels, and delivery risk with Finance and Legal. You will resolve launch blockers with Engineering, verify first billing, close the software order with the account executive, and report partner offtake value, metered GPU-hours against commitment, and booked vCluster ARR separately.

This role could be a fit for you if you bring:

  • Capacity deals you closed and carried into production: You have personally sourced and closed at least two capacity agreements (GPU capacity, inference services, or comparable cloud contracts with a minimum spend), and at least one reached paid production. You led buyer and provider teams from negotiation to first billing.

  • Leadership across providers or regions: 12+ years in cloud business development, partnerships, or infrastructure sales, or equivalent experience leading a business of comparable scope. You have carried a revenue target, built pipeline from scratch, and grown usage or recurring revenue across providers or regions.

  • Access to buyers and suppliers: You can name the first three inference buyers you would call and reach the people who can reserve GPUs. You understand how founders and ISV leaders fund production as cloud credits expire and traffic grows.

  • A matchmaking process others can run: You have launched a capacity planning, partner referral, or workload placement system that field teams adopted, including how competing claims on GPUs get resolved.

  • Forecasting and executive judgment: You have compared a demand forecast with actual consumption, and your analysis has led a provider or infrastructure executive to add, defer, or reallocate capacity.

  • Technical and financial fluency: You know NVIDIA GPUs, inference developer tools, and Kubernetes. With a solutions architect, you can benchmark latency and throughput under peak traffic and size a reservation, and you can show a CFO how cost per million tokens and provider margin change at half the forecast traffic.

Bonus points for:

  • Adjacent backgrounds: GPU cloud sales, compute procurement for a model provider, or capacity partnerships at an inference platform.

  • Compute marketplace experience: Operating a compute marketplace or working with NCPs participating in AICP.

  • Startup program sourcing: Sourcing startups through AWS Activate or Google for Startups.

  • Advanced degree: An MBA or advanced technical degree, or equivalent practical experience.

About vCluster Labs

We're the #1 platform for AI infrastructure, trusted by the world's fastest-growing AI cloud builders. We're a venture-backed startup that's raised over $28M from top-tier investors including Khosla Ventures (first investor in OpenAI, GitLab, Stripe, and DoorDash), and we're in a hyper-growth phase looking for motivated people to join our team. Our headquarters are in San Francisco (Salesforce Tower), but our team is distributed around the globe with a remote-first culture.

We give AI Cloud providers and AI factories a hyperscaler-like experience on their own GPU infrastructure. Our platform runs the full stack an operator needs, from bare metal provisioning and node lifecycle management up through managed Kubernetes, Slurm, Ray, and inference clusters, so they can turn raw GPUs into cluster products they can sell in days instead of spending 12+ months building it themselves. Today we power over 100,000 GPUs and 1 million CPUs across 50+ AI clouds and Fortune 500 companies, backed by a team of 40+ infrastructure engineers who build alongside our customers rather than just shipping them software.

We're the company behind vCluster, the open source technology for tenant isolation on Kubernetes, with 11,000+ GitHub stars and 40M+ tenant clusters created since 2021. Open source is part of our DNA. At KubeCon North America 2025, we launched our Infrastructure Tenancy Platform for AI, a Kubernetes-native framework built for running AI, ML, and GPU-intensive workloads anywhere, with an NVIDIA-validated reference architecture for DGX systems.

Benefits

We offer the following benefits:

The Group Head of PMO is responsible for leading and overseeing the Group's project management function across all subsidiaries, business units, and geographical markets within the Insurance & Investments sector.

The role establishes group-wide project governance, portfolio management standards, delivery frameworks, and performance monitoring systems to ensure that strategic projects and transformation initiatives are executed effectively. The position provides centralized oversight of project priorities, budgets, resources, risks, dependencies, and expected business outcomes.

Working closely with the Group CEO, executive leadership, subsidiary CEOs, and business heads, the Group Head of PMO ensures that all major projects support the organization's strategic growth, operational efficiency, digital transformation, and long-term business objectives.

Group PMO Strategy & Governance

Risk, Compliance & Quality Management

  • Coordinate with group risk, compliance, legal, and internal audit functions.
  • Ensure projects comply with internal policies, governance standards, and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Establish contingency and mitigation plans for critical projects and strategic programs.

Performance Reporting & Benefits Realization

  • Develop group-wide project dashboards, performance reports, and executive presentations.
  • Monitor project delivery against approved scope, budgets, timelines, milestones, and quality standards.
  • Track financial benefits, operational improvements, and ROI from strategic initiatives.

  • Recommend strategic interventions to improve project execution and delivery performance.

Stakeholder & Subsidiary Management

  • Work closely with subsidiary CEOs, managing directors, business unit heads, project sponsors, and program directors.
  • Facilitate group-level project steering committees and portfolio review meetings.
  • Coordinate project planning and delivery across subsidiaries and corporate functions.
  • Manage relationships with external consultants, technology vendors, contractors, and implementation partners.
  • Ensure consistent communication, accountability, and reporting across all Group entities.

Leadership & PMO Capability Development

  • Lead and develop the Group PMO team, including PMO directors, project managers, project analysts, and project controls specialists.
  • Establish PMO structures, responsibilities, and reporting relationships across subsidiaries.
  • Develop project management training, mentoring, and capability-building initiatives.
  • Promote a culture of accountability, transparency, collaboration, and delivery excellence.
  • Drive continuous improvement in project management maturity across the organization.

3. Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Finance, Project Management, Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field.
  • MBA or Master's degree in Project Management, Business Strategy, Finance, or a relevant discipline preferred.
  • 12–15+ years of progressive experience in project management, program management, portfolio management, or enterprise transformation.
  • At least 5 years in a senior PMO leadership position overseeing multiple business units, subsidiaries, or large project portfolios.
  • Experience in insurance, reinsurance, banking, investment management, asset management, wealth management, or diversified financial services.
